Join us for the VeloPigs Beer and Bicycle Social Club’s 6th annual Oink At The Moon! This event is a non-competitive NIGHT GRAVEL ride taking place on the rural farm roads of western Loudoun County. 

 

Oink at the Moon Roots! 

Oink At The Moon originally began as a single, standalone charity ride in October 2020. VeloPigs’ founder, Kasey Clark, attempted to ride every gravel road in Loudoun County (over 285 miles!) in a single day. The ride was a success and raised significant funds for America’s Routes, a Loudoun-based non-profit whose mission is to protect and preserve these historic roads.

 

In 2021, to pay homage to Kasey’s big ride, the VeloPigs organized a night gravel century and opened it to club members. Each year since, Oink At The Moon has continued to grow into one of the highlights of the Loudoun County cycling calendar. It is a true grassroots gravel event, and we would love for you to come share this experience with us!

 

This year we are again being hosted by longtime VeloPig and ride leader, Brian Holesapple. He is graciously allowing us to start and end our ride at his property near Philomont.

 

Even if you’ve ridden Loudoun’s gravel before (perhaps every Saturday morning with the VeloPigs), riding at night completely changes the experience. Prepare for an exhilarating new adventure, traversing some of the lost corners of the county and camaraderie you can only find on a ride like this!

 

Ride Details

  • Routes and parking information will be emailed to you when you register.

  • The ride will take place on open roads, both gravel and paved. 

  • The ride starts at 6:30 pm, approximately half an hour before sunset, and will finish well after dark.

  • Participants are expected to follow all rules of the road and act as responsible stewards for the sport of cycling. 

  • The route will be unmarked, though GPS routes will be emailed upon registration. 

  • Road conditions will range from hardpack (almost as smooth as pavement) to sometimes deep, loose gravel with potholes and washboard. 

  • We recommend at least a 32mm tire width, though 38+ mm is ideal. We also recommend tubeless tires - changing a flat in the dark is not easy!

 

Route Options

This year, we have three route options (63 miles, 46 miles, and 30 miles – routes will be sent when you register). Unlike our Saturday club rides, these groups will not have ride leaders and are NOT no-drop. Meaning, these are drop rides. Riders are encouraged, but not required, to stick with their ride group.

The VeloPigs follow the “Mullet Protocol” for all our rides: 

  • Business at the front, party at the back. 

    • The Business is 63 miles, and the group will ride at an average speed of 16+ mph. 

    • Business Casual is 46 miles and will average 14.5-16 mph. 

    • Party Pace is 30 miles and will average 12-14.5 mph. 

  • Please register for the route and pace that will best suit your riding abilities.

  • Riders are asked to stage 5-10 minutes before the ride begins. 

  • Groups will roll out at 5-minute intervals to avoid congesting the small roads with too many riders.

 

Rest Stops

  • There are no designated rest stops, though each route passes by at least one convenience store:

    • The Business: Middleburg Safeway at mile 11, The Plains Sunoco at mile 29, and Middleburg Safeway again at mile 45.

    • Business Casual: Middleburg Safeway at mile 11, and Middleburg Safeway again at mile 29.

    • Party Pace: Purcellville 7-Eleven at mile 21.

  • Riders are expected to bring their own hydration and nutrition, and/or money to purchase more along the way.

     

Most Importantly - Food & Drink!

  • Pizza, beer (21+), and VeloPigs swag are included with entry will be provided after the ride. 

 

The Fine Print

  • Riders are expected to have appropriate fitness, equipment, and bike handling skills to complete their selected route.
  • Helmets, headlights, and taillights are REQUIRED!
    • We recommend staying with a riding buddy in case of mechanical or light issues.
  • Mechanical support will be provided before the ride by VeloPigs’ bike shop sponsor, Plum Grove Cyclery.
  • SAG support will be available for riders who experience mechanical difficulties and are unable to complete the ride.
  • Registration may be edited or transferred at no charge up until the day before the event, however refunds will not be granted.
  • If you would like to participate in this ride but are unable to cover the registration cost, please contact the Event Director.

 

Lastly, some friendly advice (because this has been an issue every year): It may be warm at the beginning of the ride, but it will get cold quickly when the sun sets! 

DRESS FOR THE COLD TEMPS AT THE END OF THE RIDE, NOT THE WARM TEMPS AT THE BEGINNING. Trust us on this….

The cyclocross cycling event is slightly different as the season runs across two calendar years starting in the fall and ending in February of the following year. Therefore CX race age is determined by an athletes racing age on DEC 31st of the year that Cyclocross season ends. CX season starts in September and goes until the end of February. A quick way to remember CX racing age is your current race age +1.

Please visit our website for venue information and racing requirements. https://www.utcx.net

UTCX is a USA Cycling-sanctioned series and follows USA Cycling’s Competition Category Policy.

Any UTCX category that is not designated as a Women’s or Junior category is open to all riders, regardless of sex assigned at birth. For the 2026 season, this gives riders 10 categories open to everyone, subject to the age and USA Cycling category requirements listed for each race.

Women’s categories follow USA Cycling’s eligibility requirements. Junior categories are based on age and sex category.

Our goal is simple: there is a place for everyone to race at UTCX, and all riders are welcome.

Farm event rules:

1. NO DOGS – Big, little, pure, mutt we love them all, but the only dogs allowed are the family farm dogs. THIS INCLUDES EVERYONE, NOT JUST CAMPERS. 

2. No open fires. You can bring your portable grills or campfire rings but no open campfires. 

3. No smoking anything.

4. Kids supervised – You’re invited and encouraged to bring your entire family to our events. We require that children have adult supervision while on the farm at all times and you, as the parent or guardian, must provide this supervision. There are 2 ponds and there will be no lifeguard on duty. Swimming is at your own risk.

RE: Kids in the pond – This is a big attraction for the youngsters and a great way for them to spend some time. However, please be aware that the boats and floating dock are the Oesterlings property and they must be treated with care. Abuse of these items or any other property will not be tolerated. Destruction of property will result in immediate ejection from the property.

5. Keep it quiet during quiet times. Quiet hours are 10pm – 7am. There will be plenty of time for you to be rowdy and loud cheering on the other racers. 

6. Don’t be a jerk.

7. Respect the property. For more than two decades now you’ve been pretty solid, which is why we keep inviting you all back. Please remember that the Oesterlings live here all year long, have been incredibly supportive of mountain biking and ‘cross racing on this property and are my in-laws! Please thank the Oesterlings for their hospitality whenever you have the chance.

8. DO NOT LITTER. I’m not just talking about around the venue where we will have some trash receptacles, but do not drop your used gel packs on the course. I know you’re quite sure that those used foil containers are going to weigh you down and keep you from winning, but if you’re caught littering the course you’ll be DQ’d (and that don’t mean I’m taking you out for a BliZzard). Put that packet back in your jersey pocket or under your leg band ’til the end of the race. The only place you will be allowed to drop the food wrappers is at the start/finish line/feed zone area where they must be picked up by a teammate or your support person. DO NOT LITTER or leave your unwanted trash or debris behind.

9. Pack out what you pack in. Going along really well with #9 above. Bring a big ol’ trash bag, put your garbage in your big ol’ trash bag, put your big ol’ trash bag in your car, put your car in your driveway, and put your trash in your trashcan at home. Thanks for helping us keep the place clean. Helping us with little things like this keeps the event going because it keeps my crew, my folks, my outlaws, and my wife happy!

10. We reserve the right to create and impose further rules or do whatever else we want!

EventNotes:
Join Us for an Epic Day on the Gravel!

The Jersey Gravel Grinder returns in 2026 for another unforgettable ride through the backroads, dirt lanes, and hidden gems of the Garden State. Whether you’re chasing the sunrise or chasing a new PR, this is Jersey’s own gravel adventure — and it’s calling your name. Full Event Details including planned course routes are up on RSGADVENTURES.com.

The Ride: Gravel, Grit & Glory

Our signature JGG routes deliver a perfectly mixed all-surface adventure — from smooth tarmac to gritty gravel, rugged dirt, and maybe even a bit of singletrack on the Mega & Mega XL courses. Expect 45%–75% unpaved terrain, all clearly marked with arrow signs at every turn.

Prefer tech over trail signs? You’ll also get free access to our RideWithGPS event account, with downloadable FIT and GPX files, plus visual and audio cues to guide you every pedal stroke.

Ride Your Way – Enduro Style

This isn’t just a race — it’s an experience. Compete for the fastest combined time on timed segments rather than your total ride time. You’ll see clear signage marking the Approach, Start, and End of each Strava segment, so you know exactly when to hammer and when to chill.
Go full gas or soak in the scenery — it’s your adventure, your pace.

We'll be using a GPS based App to collect teams and provide leaderboards.

Stocked Aid Stations

We’ll keep you fueled and smiling all day long.
Aid Stations every 20–30 miles will be fully stocked with:

  • GU Gels & Chews
  • Hydration Mix, Water & Coke
  • Aid Station 1 features fresh hot pancakes with maple syrup — because every great adventure deserves breakfast on the trail!
  • Aid Station 2 features hot pierogis & pickle juice
  • Plus More Rider Favorites

All stations include toilets and hand sanitizer for your comfort and convenience.

What You Get

Registration includes:

  • Custom Eastern Gravel Series Swag - Custom Sock Guy Socks & EGS Water Bottle
  • Mid-loop Hot Coffee or Espresso Stop (Adventure & Mega)
  • Post-Ride Meal & Prize Raffle Entry
  • The satisfaction of riding Jersey’s best backroads with a like-minded community of adventurers

Our raffle prizes are always top-notch — past giveaways have included helmets, tires, sunglasses, apparel, gear, and more from our amazing sponsors.

Routes

Each year, we change up the routes to keep the adventure fresh. Riders will receive final GPS files before the event.
Check out routes from past editions for a taste of what’s to come — a true mix of challenge, beauty, and pure gravel joy. (Examples from prior year below and see RSGADVENTURES.com to view 2026 planned routes.

Pricing

Our pricing structure rewards early sign-ups — and each category has limited space.
Prices increase either by date or when a ride category sells out.

Don’t just ride. Adventure.

We get it — sometimes plans change. That’s why we offer flexible options so your adventure isn’t lost.

Welcome to Lake Milton MTB Trails & NEO Retreat Center!

We are returning to Lake Milton for a second year, and this event would not be possible without the folks from Rust Belt Revival Trail Coalition and the neighbors at NEO Retreat Center. If you would like to camp Saturday night contact NEO Retreat Center to reserve a spot. please remember we are guests on this Christian retreat center property, and no alcohol is permitted on the property.

Due to road closures approach from 534!

Course Info

  • Race Course on Strava here.
  • Race start is at NEO Retreat Center, and is off limits until race day!
  • 6.3 miles per lap.
  • Can be ridden race direction every day for the week prior to race day.

Day Of Registration:

While we strongly encourage you to preregister (and greatly appreciate you doing so as it helps the event go more smoothly), there will be "day of" registration. It will be an extra $10 after 6pm Saturday evening, and will close 60 minutes before the start of your event.

 

Race day Schedule:

  • 9am registration/packet pickup opens
  • 9:30am Cat 3 Jr Novice U19-U13 & Kids race day of registration closes
  • 10am Cat3 Jr Novice U19-U13 & Kids race start
  • 11:30 am day of registration & number pickup closes.
  • 11:40 am Jr Novice podiums and riders Meeting
  • 12pm Cat 1 categories start
  • 12:40pm All remaining cat 2 and cat 3 categories start. THIS TIME IS APPROXIMATE!
  • 2:30-3pm, all podiums.
  • Adaptive racers, we may alter where in the schedule you start as we work with you and learn what works best. 

!!!!!!!Start time notes!!!!!

In an effort to offer a safer and more fun race environment for all participants we are now starting Cat 2 and Cat 3 racers after Cat 1 and E Bikes have completed one lap. This greatly reduces conflict between very fast cat 1 and E Bike racers passing novice racers by nearly eliminating lap traffic. The posted start time of 12:40m for cat 2 & 3 is approximate. We will begin releasing the remaining cat 2 & 3 waves after Cat 1 racers go through scoring. Know your wave number!

10am Cat3 Jr. Novice Races

You may have noticed that we are doing Cat3 Jr novice races early in the day and be asking "hey, what's up with that?" We want to give Jr's, and particularly novice Jr's the best race day experience we can. Separating the Jr. novice races to an earlier start allows us to do 3 things:

  • Fewer racers on course for the race.
  • For families where the one or both parents also race it gives the parents a chance to spectate and cheer their kids.
  • Novice Jr's get their own start, with more people cheering and spectating. Bring the cowbells!

USA Cycling Licenses, and NOMBS Series Championship rules & eligibility:

NOMBS is proud to be bringing a USAC sanctioned series to Ohio and be hosting the official USA Cycling Ohio MTB Championship. Partnering with USA Cycling helps us offer you a great series with structure, consistent categories & scoring, good insurance for landowners, and allows an opportunity for riders with goals outside Ohio to earn USAC points. 

USA Cycling Race Age:

 Your “race age” is the age you will be on December 31st. This rule exists so that a person does not have to change the age group they are entering partway through a race season. 

NOMBS Series Championship Eligibility rules:

  1. A rider must have a current USA Cycling License (need not reside in Ohio).
  2. Must race in the season finale race.
  3. Scored on best 5 races.
  4. In the event of a points tie the season final race is the tie breaker.

Complete series rules can be found here.

EventNotes:
The Tour of the Rio Grande Bicycle Century will not be an organized mass event in 2026.

For locals who are familiar with the South Valley area near the start / finish, there's been a lot of road work and construction. We have been talking with Bernalillo County and NMDOT for the past couple months in regards to the ride / permitting. They say with what is planned for Rio Bravo Blvd and its intersection with 2nd street, they cannot guarantee they will approve our permitting. They described how the state of the construction will make the road unsafe for cyclists. It is with this information I have chosen to make the event virtual.

A virtual event is one that doesn't have a particular ride date, start time or support outside of ridewithgps directions fournd on our website www.torgbc.com. This is being done so that the event holds its 4th / last Sunday of September spot on public calendars. It also gives fans of the ride the option to use the ridewithgps to find a place to park away from the construction, and attempt a part or all of the ride. There are a number of local businesses on the way that have food and beverage and they would love your support.

We did think about moving the start / finish to make the ride happen and we came to the conclusion to not change the ride in fear of ruining the experience.

Registration for the virtual tour is $5 or $20. Both options have fees and tax. The $20 dollar option will include a shirt and stickers for the virtual tour 2026 and local sponsor perks with shipping included. These will start being shipped in June and sent as they are ordered with an estimated two week turnaround time.

Online registration is open until 11:59pm MST Sunday September 27th.

Categories.CategoryName: Gravel Ride through Pownal, VT and surrounding areas

EventNotes:
The Tour de Pownal is back, thanks to the efforts of the Solomon Wright Public Library, Town of Pownal, HooRWA, Faith Church, Pownal Historical Society, Parks and Rec Committee, and the Pownal Rescue Squad! 

This is event free to register. It is not a race. Take your time, take lots of pictures, and have fun. 

Donations to the Pownal Rescue Squad can be made at Support PRS — Pownal Rescue Squad. 

Join the Bike Hub in exploring some of Pownal's historic sites! There will be two routes with a shorter 8-mile ride available and a 30-mile route highlighting some of the important sites along the way. 

Some areas of interest:
1. Pownal Center Historic District
2. Mooar-Wright Home
4. Clayton Park
5. Quarry Hill Trail
6. Witch Trial Historic Marker (and general store)
7. Peckham Farm
… and more!
 
Food: On Center Street, you will find All Belgian Waffles Food Truck! 
 
Highlights- a nature walk to the Hoosick River and tour the historic Moar Wright House, with refreshments, and kid's activities. 
 
There will be an aid station and support vehicle for the longer route. Route links will be emailed after registration, and riders kept updated on any changes. For more information, please email jess.rice@ourbikehub.org
 

Route information:

There are two routes to choose from. There is a recreational rider friendly 8-mile ride through Pownal.

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/56562221

The longer ride will appeal to the experienced gravel rider with 30 miles of gravel roads, climbing, and satisfying descents.  There will be aid stations and the Bike Hub Van will follow for support. 

https://ridewithgps.com/routes/53780900

EventName: 2026 Greylock Go Around 50K Mountain Bike Fundraiser
EventNotes:
Circumnavigate the highest point in Massachusetts at the 2026 Greylock Go Around 50K, a Mountain Bike Fundraiser for Thunderbolt Ski Runners:

  • Saturday October 3, 2025
  • $75 for non-members, $50 for members
  • Start Greylock Glen Outdoor Center and Finish at Greylock Glen Gazebo
  • 7:30am-8:30am sign in
  • Start time: 9:00am
  • Mountain Bike required
  • Riders must wear a properly fitted helmet
  • Basic toolkit (multitool, tube, pump, CO2) encouraged
  • 150 registration cap
  • 3 Aid Stations on course with food and hydration and limited tech support

Course GPX file will be available the week prior to the event.  Rough course breakdown:  31 miles/50K, 4,100 feet of climbing.  20% Paved, 50% forest road/double track and 30% single track.  A MOUNTAIN BIKE IS REQUIRED!

Proceeds of the event benefit ongoing trail development and stewardship around Mt. Greylock, including active trail building grants.

Estimated moving time: 3.5 - 5.5 hours.

Strava Route: https://www.strava.com/routes/3006400090346181148

Trailforks Route: https://www.trailforks.com/route/greylock-go-around-50k?activitytype=1&z=11.3&lat=42.64540&lon=-73.18573&content=trails,labels,nst,poi,directory,polygon,waypoint,routes_featured

Our 6th annual 

CIDER DONUT BIKE TOUR 

October 3, 2026

NEW PALTZ / MILTON / MARLBORO

“ROAD EDITION”


New Route / Quicker Pace / Hilly Course

Different Farms / Yummy Donuts / Fun Afterparty 

 

WHICH FARM WILL GET THE 

DELICIOUS DONUT AWARD THIS YEAR???

 

Details about the 2026 ride:

  • Road Ride visiting local farms to taste cider donuts

  • 36 mile ride with options to join or leave the ride at any point

  • Average speed 16-20mph. 2000 feet of climbing with rolling hills

  • Route will be on open roads in the New Paltz, Milton and Malboro area

  • The Ride with GPS route is HERE

  • Meeting location, parking, start and finish point is Twin Star Orchards

  • 8:50am Welcome remarks 

  • 9:00am sharp ride begins behind the White Bronco lead out vehicle

    • Police assistance possible at a few major road crossings

  • We will visit these farms in this order:

    • Twin Star Orchards

    • Minard’s Farm

    • Weed Orchard (not confirmed yet)

    • Locust Grove  

    • Dubois Farm

    • Twin Star Orchard afterparty

      • Donuts, Cider, Pizza, Burgers, Music

      • Hyperice Recovery Lounge with recovery boots

    • Delicious Donut Award point system to rate the donuts

    • Registration opens September 1

      • Fill out Athlete Information Form and complete the online waiver 

  • Registration is $50 per rider

    • Includes a ticket for a donut or apple at each farm

    • CDBT water bottle

    • One cider drink at the finish

    • 10 minute recovery boot session

  • If registering for multiple riders, please register separately 

  • Additional donut tasting/food purchasing fees at each farm are covered by each rider on site 

    • Food at Twin Star Orchard afterparty is not included in registration

      We will aim to stay together as a group, stopping for 20 - 30 minutes at each farm and on to the next one

      Hand the ticket to the counter, receive donut or apple, taste, enjoy… and onward.  

  • Please ride with due regard for your surroundings, other cyclists and vehicles on the roadway

  • Ride safely and obey all traffic laws. Helmets are advised. Ride single file and to the right

  • Road or gravel bikes are recommended. Some gravel roads to farm entrances

  • Riders of all levels are welcome but this is a bit more moderate to advanced rider level with hills

  • No dogs please. Families and pups can meet at Twin Star for the afterparty

  • Ride is self supported regarding bike maintenance, flat tires and nutrition

    • We will have a water cooler for refills at farm stops

  • Ride is rain or shine

    • We will ride if it is raining light

    • Moderate to heavy continuous rain will cancel the ride

      • Registration fees could be carried over to new rescheduled date if it is postponed 

  • We are looking forward to another fun ride with you all!

  • Enjoy the beautiful views, pretty fall colors and social outdoor experience!

EventName: Charm City Cross - USCX Series UCI C1/C2
EventNotes:
PRESENTED BY WAGNER ROOFING

                          

CHARM CITY CROSS TECHNICAL GUIDE 2026 AVAILABLE ON CHARMCITYCROSS,COM

Saturday October 3rd & Sunday October 4th 2026

Druid Hill Park Zoo Mansion Lawn---- Baltimore, Maryland USA

The Venue & Event

Druid Hill Park is a beautiful, historic 745 acre urban park established in 1859. In 2026 Charm City Cross will mark the 22nd annual race and our 11th year as a UCI sanctioned race. This is a two day Category 1 and 2 UCI and USA Cycling cyclocross event. The event will be held under UCI regulations and USA Cycling Permit # 15999. UCI scale of penalties and USAC penalties will apply.

Registration-

Registration Fees:  

$70 for UCI Elite events

$30 for Juniors and Non-UCI Juniors

$65for UCI Junior Men and Junior Women

$65 for all other events except category 5  

SPECIAL NOTES:  This is a rolling entry fee.   prices increase $10  beginning on September 16th

Small World Championships Free

Online registration closes on Wednesday , September 29th at 11:59pm

There is also a nominal fee to register online with BikeReg.

No mail-in registration and NO REFUNDS after August 31st 2026

On-Site Late Registration may be available for non-UCI classes, however, we urge you to register online to avoid the additional $10 same-day registration fee. UCI racers must pre-register.

Friday night 10/2 from 6-9 at Union Craft Brewing we will have pre-registered packets available for pickup (non-UCI races only). 

The registration pavilion will open by 6:30 am and closes 30 minutes before each race. 

NOTE for UCI races registration and number pick up closes 1 hour before each event.

 

Friday October 2nd Schedule

Pro Teams are encouraged to set up Friday morning and afternoon.  

Pre-Ride 

There will be preride Friday.   Racers found on course prior to 4:30 and after 6:30pm can be denied participation for the weekends events.  HEAVY RAIN OR WEATHER CAN CANCEL THIS PRE-RIDE

 

Directions to Druid Hill Park (Important Update from years past)

Google Maps: To get to the east park entrance please use 810 Wyman Park Dr, Baltimore, MD 21211 

Directions from points North and West of Baltimore

The directions below are from I-83.  You can get to I-83 in the following ways:

From Philly: I-95 to I-695 to I-83 South 

From Central PA:  I-83 South

From WV:  I-70E to I-695N to I-83 South

 

Directions from points North of Baltimore

 I-83 (South) to Exit 7 (east) to W 28th St.  

-Turn left at the light onto Sisson St.

-Turn left at the light onto Wyman Park Dr to enter the park, continue on East Dr past the tennis/basketball courts and look for parking.

-Please remember to lock your vehicle and keep valuables out of plain sight.

Directions from points South of Baltimore

I-95N to Exit 53 I-395N toward ML King Blvd

-Continue on ML King Blvd

-Turn LEFT on N Howard St

-Turn left onto W 24th St.

-Turn right onto Sisson St

-Make a left at the light onto Wyman Park Dr to enter the park, continue on East Dr past the tennis/basketball courts and look for parking.

Public Parking (For General Parking- You are not permitted to park on the grass)

General parking is provided on the roads surrounding the venue. These roads are Beechwood Dr, Swann Dr, Red Rd and East Drive (Red hashing on the map).  Please, park as one would normally on heavily traveled roads. Please Do Not Park in the Grass. Follow all parking signs and laws.  Be aware that parking is limited, so carpooling is recommended and arrive at least 2 hours before your start time.  DO NOT leave valuables unattended or in plain sight, and secure your vehicle as you see fit.

DROP OFF:   PLEASE TAKE NOTE. 

This year, a secure drop-off point will be provided for Pro Parking, Club row, and VIP.  This drop-off will be located at the base of the grass triangle at the main entrance to the venue, Mansion House Drive.  This is only for equipment, rider, or VIP drop-off or pick-up.  You can not leave your vehicle for more than 10 mins at this spot. Vehicle access to Pro parking and Club row will close at 10:00 AM. Meaning NO vehicle will be allowed to access these areas after 10AM.  Vehicles may leave but will not be allowed to reenter.  This is for the safety of the races and the overall success and viability of the race in the future. Thank you for understanding. 


 

Pro Parking:

Pro parking will be available for vehicle access Friday all day, Saturday 6-10 AM, and Sunday 6-10 AM.  After 10 AM on Saturday and Sunday, NO vehicle access will be available for PRO team parking. Racers or staff arriving after 10 AM will be required to use the secure drop-off point located at the base of the grass triangle at the main entrance of the venue. You can not leave your vehicle for more than 10 mins at this point. This is for the safety of the races and the overall success and viability of the race in the future. Thank you for understanding. 

 

Club Row:

Club row parking will be available for vehicle access Friday all day, Saturday 6-10 AM, and Sunday 6-10 AM.  We strongly encourage you to drop off and set up your Club Row tents on Friday. There will be overnight security but please do not leave anything of value with your tent. After 10 AM on Saturday and Sunday, NO vehicle access will be available for Club row parking. Racers or spectators arriving after 10 AM will be required to use the secure drop-off point located at the base of the grass triangle at the main entrance of the venue. You can not leave your vehicle for more than 10 mins at this spot. This is for the safety of the races and the overall success and viability of the race in the future. Thank you for understanding. 

VIP Parking will be at the bottom of Mansion Drive. If you have not worked out a VIP pass, do not expect to get one the day of racing.

There will be ADA accessible parking near Registration. 

Event General Parking is FREE and is on East Dr., Red Rd. and Grove Rd. Do Not expect to park on Mansion Dr nor Swan Drive.  Please Do Not Park on the grass unless directed by city park staff! Please remember to lock your vehicle and keep valuables out of plain sight.

Licensing Requirements

The UCI Elite Men/U23 Men, UCI Elite Women/U23 Women must have a current International License. A domestic USAC license is acceptable for all other categories. All racers must have a current cycling license.

One-day beginner licenses are available for $10 on-site for Cat 5 racers only.  

One day licenses for Categories 1-4 must be purchased online at USA cycling.org.

This is a traditional Charm City Cross course looping through the historic DRUID HILL PARK Baltimore Zoo Mansion House Lawn.  A Combination of pavement, grass, dirt and obstacles will be experienced. Course is roughly 1.8 miles

Course Map

Course Inspection and Warm-up

The course will be open for inspection and warm-up approximately 10 minutes prior to each event.  The officials will make an announcement when the course has been opened for inspection.  Warming up on the course during an event is strictly prohibited and will not be tolerated. Violations can result in disqualification. We suggest you inspect the course at least two slots before your race as you will need to get to the starting grid 15 minutes before your start time for staging.

There will be a UCI only course warm up period at 12:10 to 12:30. this is UCI ONLY.

IMPORTANT UCI START INFORMATION

Uci Elite riders please note the following:  

Start Line Protocol

Racers must report to the holding pen adjacent to the starting grid for staging 15 minutes before the start of their race. If you arrive late you will be staged at the next available position. 

Call-Up Protocol

Staging Procedure Riders shall be staged by the rider's assigned bib number.  Walk-up riders will be assigned remaining bib numbers on a first-come, first-served basis.  All riders will line up in the order of their numbers, filling gaps as allowed by the officials/callers.  Staging will fill the start grid as specified in the USAC rulebook start grid.

Staging Order for amateur races will be based on the most recent CrossResults.com ranking and USCX standings, using the following criteria:

The top 8 riders in the current USCX series standings who are pre-registered will be staged on the front row.

Remaining riders will be staged by CrossResults.com ranking.

All categories will reserve four spots in the third row, which are to be used for promoters’ discretion call-ups.

The first race of each year shall stage racers by their CrossResults.com ranking.

Those classes consisting of only cat 4/5 men or cat 4/5 women are staged by order of registration - starting with those who registered earliest.

UCI races will be called up per UCI regulations.

Feeding: 

For UCI races only:  No feeding is permitted. Riders are advised to add a water bottle on their bikes if necessary. Accepting hand-ups from spectators – including bottles, cans or money – is not permitted and will result in disqualification. No alcohol is permitted on the course or in the technical area.

For USAC races only: Rule 4A15: Feeding is generally not permitted unless specifically authorized by the Chief Referee. If authorized, there is normally no feeding in the first two and final two laps of the race. The location of feeding will be determined by the Chief Referee in conjunction with the Race Organization

Lapped Riders in UCI Events (UCI Rule 5.1.051): All riders lapped before the final lap must leave the race the next time they cross the finish line. The rider will be given a placing if he or she was lapped more than half way through the race.  A rider who is lapped on the final lap shall be stopped at the beginning of the finishing straight line and shall be given a placing on the basis of his or her position. Additionally, Commissaires may pull riders who are behind by more than 80% of the leader's lap time. 

Lapped Riders in Non-UCI Events: Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leaders. Riders in danger of being lapped must yield to oncoming racers and are not to interfere with their progress or trail behind them. 

Pit

There will be one double-sided pit on the course.  Only authorized personnel are allowed access to the pit and must have their pit pass displayed at all times.  Pit passes will be distributed at registration to each competitor (one per entrant) in UCI events (Elite Men, Elite Women & Junior Men and Junior Women).

Pit Box assigments for UCI events will be done in advance by the PCP. Allocation will be available at check in.

In non-UCI events, only those working the pit will be allowed. The pit official will have the authority to remove anyone that is interfering with the proper functioning of the pit.

We will have bike racks in the Pit.  These are for racers that are currently racing, not for storing your equipment all day. Please remove your equipment immediately following your race to make room for others.

Bike washdown for active races will be approximately 50m from the pit with two pressure washers available.

Note: Additional bike washing will be available near registration for racers after their event if the weather dictates it.

Equipment

No flat bars or tires wider than 33mm will be allowed in UCI events (Elite Men, Elite Women). Officials will check tires in the holding pen prior to the start of the UCI races.  .

For racers participating in the singlespeed events, they may either ride a true singlespeed bike (one chainring and one freewheeling cog) or may also ziptie a SRAM-equipped drop bar bike into one rideable gear. Zip ties should be left untrimmed and can be obtained at the registration table. No ziptieing of Shimano- or Campagnolo-equipped drop bar bikes. We encourage elite (non-UCI) racers to adhere to the spirit of the discipline.

Anti-Doping

Anti-doping is under the control of USADA and ITA in accordance with UCI regulations.  The location of the anti-doping area will be located  directly after the line to the right

Immediately following the completion of each race on both October  2nd and 3rd, the top 3 riders must proceed to the podium area. This includes ALL amateur and UCI events. EventNotes:
If you enjoy leisurely bike rides with a wide variety of scenery, join us while we explore Idaho's longest rail trail on this two day 85 mile ride from alpine meadows to desert canyons.  Located in southwest Idaho, the Weiser River Trail runs from Weiser to nearly New Meadows along the former Pacific and Idaho Northern rail line. The railroad corridor is owned by Friends of Weiser River Trail (FWRT), the sponsor of this event.  FWRT is dedicated to providing a unique recreational opportunity along the trail including developed trailheads and a campground to assist trail users. OctoberTrek is an opportunity to experience our rail trail with all the amenities of a supported ride and helps you meet new cycling friends in a noncompetitive atmosphere.

The entry fee includes shuttle for the rider and bike, event shirt, meals, campground tent site and hot spring soak, luggage transportation, refreshments, sweep, and sag support.  Before you register, see the October Trek participant information on https://weiserrivertrail.org/events for more details, including video and photos from past events.

The rider registration fee includes a T-shirt. Riders registering after we place the order on September 20 will receive a shirt at the event only if we have extras available.  The shirt order deadline is September 20.  We will determine the shirt color from what is available from the manufacturer in September.

If you have nonriders accompanying you, additional fees apply to them for camping and hot spring use and each meal the nonrider chooses to attend.  Nonrider meals are limited to Saturday lunch, Saturday supper (includes hot spring and tent camping), and Sunday breakfast. Nonriders are not eligible for Sunday lunch because it will be on the trail.  Contact us for breakout of costs at weiserrivertrail@gmail.com.

Event registration is for tent camping at Mundo Hot Springs. There are optional RV site, a 6 bunk hostel, hotel style room or cabin available at additional cost. Reservations may be made directly with Mundo Hot Spring at 208-257-3849.

Consider becoming a member of Friends of Weiser River Trail. This National Recreation Trail is totally supported by our members along with donations and grants. Members receive updates on trail news and events through our newsletter. Visit us at http://weiserrivertrail.org/membership-%2F-donations for membership links.

This is the 17th year of Going the Distance! This annual bike ride raises much needed funds to support the Boys & Girls Club of Brattleboro. 

The pavement rides are 40, 60, or 75 miles in distance, supported by rest areas in Turners Falls and Greenfield as well as a support vehicle. These rides travel down Route 142 through Vernon and enters Massachusetts, continuing on beautiful country roads until the first rest stop in Turners Falls. From there the 40-mile riders return to Brattleboro, while those on the 60 & 75 mile rides continue through more gorgeous country roads, with the second rest stop along the Green River in Greenfield, MA where lunch is provided. The final leg of the ride brings you back to the Club, where a celebration awaits at our NEYT After Party!

We also have gravel routes available. The 26.8 mile and 38.7 mile Gravel and Gravel Plus routes through Dummerston and Putney offer outstanding riding on quiet New England back roads! With both rides starting and ending at the idyllic Rt. 30 covered bridge riders will immediately be immersed in a quintessential gravel ride.

The 38.7 mile Gravel Plus ride is not only the longer of the two offerings, but the tougher as well. With nearly 5,000 ft. of climbing (and descending!) over all possible terrain (Class IV roads, abandoned roads and single track...as well as loads of beautiful quiet back roads) this ride will challenge the strongest of riders. But don't get too scared -- it is all rideable on a good gravel bike. We recommend 35mm tires or larger.

The 26.8 mile Gravel ride offers much the same as the longer route, but it is shorter, has less climbing and there are no technical Class IV roads, abandoned roads and single track. If you have a bike with 35mm or larger tires suitable for quiet, beautiful tree lined back roads you are properly equipped. Just bring the lungs and legs to ride the mileage with nearly 2,975 ft. of elevation -- some hard but satisfying climbs (You did it!) and the always fun descents -- cruising down the most wonderful roads imaginable.  Then the Gravel ride is for you!
 
 
E-bikes? Sure, bring the motor...we're not snobs! There will be plenty of riders probably wishing they had your e-bike...
Whether you see these rides as a piece of cake or you have doubts you can handle it, there will be support vehicles and a rest stop at Putney School with lunch and "carbs to carry" to fuel you and assist you.
After the ride take a dip in the West River to cool off and then head to NEYT on Flat Street for an awesome After Party!

EventName: PGC250 Passage to the Past Bicycle Tour
EventNotes:
PGC250 invites you to take a commemorative bicycle tour of iconic historic sites to honor America’s Semiquincentennial in Prince George’s County as we explore the theme of “We the People.” 

WHEN: Saturday, October 3, 2026 from 10:00 a.m. – 2:00 p.m.
WHERE: Patuxent River Park Pavilion, 16000 Croom Airport Road, Upper Marlboro, MD 20772
LENGTH: 25 miles, a cue sheet and route map will be provided
ROUTE: https://ridewithgps.com/routes/56357303 

ABOUT THE RIDE

PGC250 created a bicycle tour for you to learn about the vast array of iconic historic sites in rural Prince George’s County while enjoying a bicycle trip. The route stops at iconic sites that have featured in the history of Prince Georges County such as Selby’s Landing, Columbia Airfield, Nottingham, St. Thomas’ Church, the Rural Life Museum and the Merkle Natural Resources Management Area. Riders will meet at the Patuxent River Park Pavilion and follow THIS ROUTE. (The route may be revised depending on road conditions at the time of the event. All roads are paved, though rural roads may be rough in places. Printed cue sheets indicating the turns will be available at the event.) Experienced volunteer cyclists will ride along with us to assist riders and site leaders will greet riders at each stop to provide information about the history and significance of the sites. Refreshments will be provided at selected stops, and at the end of the tour, which will end with closing remarks. This event is funded by a SHINE grant and was built in partnership with Sankofa Impact. Thank you to volunteers from the Oxon Hill Bicycle and Trail Club for their help and advice.

ABOUT PGC250

The United States Semiquincentennial is the 250th Anniversary of the Declaration of Independence which occurred on July 4, 2026. In 2023, Gov. Moore authorized the Maryland 250 Commission and charged it with developing, encouraging, and executing an inclusive observance of the 250th Anniversary that recognizes all Marylanders’ struggle for life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness before, during, and after the Revolution, and identified three themes – history, civics, and service. 

In Prince George’s County, Anacostia Trails Heritage Area (ATHA), the non-profit management entity of the county’s state-certified cultural tourism district, and PG Parks in the Maryland-National Capital Parks and Planning Commission created PGC250.org to create a space for conversation and collaboration to spark ideas and partnerships to creatively illustrate and interpret our region’s contributions to American history. The theme for Prince George’s Commemoration is “We the People.”

But…What is cyclocross anyway?!

Weellll…it's kinda like if a road bike and a mountain bike and a cross country running event all got mashed together!

Cyclocross is the best spectator friendly cycling event there is. ‘Cross races are held on short 1.5 to 2 mile laps that will mostly consist of grass and sometimes mud but can include sand, artificial barriers, hills, off camber sections, forced runs, and just about any dumb thing we can find in the park to make the race more fun to do but also to watch! We strive to make the race fun for everyone that comes out; from beginners and youth racers to the most experienced elite racers in Arkansas but especially to spectators! SHAM endeavors to make as much of the race course visible from as many spots along the way as possible, but especially at the start/finish line so you can cheer on  your friends and family and all the other racers out for a fun day in the sun…or mud…or maybe snow…but almost definitely sand and grass!

The 67 mile route has a good mix of gravel and pavement with some difficult climbs.   You will be rolling thru some of the most scenic countryside Ohio has to offer.  Tires recommendation at least a 32mm gravel tire.  We previewed the course on bikes and our GPS had us at over 6,000 of elevation gain.  The difficult part of the course is from mile 15 - 60 with over 50% gravel total. There will be 2 aid stations with Water & Nutrition.

Description

The ROJR is a “gentleman’s race,” and spans several counties that offer some of the best gravel roads in the state.  You will meander past scenic farms, through shady glens and into areas so dense and deserted you will be sure you took a wrong turn! To finish this route, trust your GPS. Keep a close eye on the weather as well as we’ve seen sleet and 70’s for this event. October weather is uncertain if anything.

The ROJR 40 can be done as an individual event or as a team of three or four. There will be several challenges along the way for time bonuses. 


Check in starts at 7:30 a.m. 
The ride honors the life of Jeremy Grimm. Grimm was a Cat I racer who lost his life in 2017 in a bicycle/truck accident. He left a wife and two daughters. 

 

Food

Light breakfast from 8:00 - 8:45 am

3 aid stations (water, nutrition)

Lunch/Dinner from 12:30 - 3:00    Featuring Chicken BBQ and cold beverages from Bowman Beverages

RULES

There will be plenty of circumstances along the course that will not be covered in the rules. When these circumstances arise, code-of-conduct best practices apply. Let's honor each other as gentlemen and gentlewomen. 

To be considered an official finishing team, and to be eligible for the grand prize and trophy, your team must complete the entire 40 mile course. If your team makes a wrong turn the team must go back to where the team left the route and continue from there. The ROJR 2026 course presents challenges throughout the race! Any portion of the map left unridden will disqualify the team from any awards.

Your team's time will stop when the third member crosses the finish line.

The underlying spirit of this event is to have fun while challenging yourself alongside good friends. The course terrain serves as a team motivator for overcoming obstacles together.

BE THE REASON SOMEBODY FINISHES THE RACE, NOT THE REASON SOMEBODY DOESN'T.

ROJR ON EVERYBODY!

 

FAQs

How does my team register for The ROJR 2026?

We ask that the Team Captain comes up with a team name and registers the team on bikereg.com/rojr Each additional team member can then register and pay separately under the team name

Individuals complete the registration

 

Are there ID or minimum age requirements to enter the event?

No ID requirements. This is not a USA Cycling sanctioned event.

 

What are my transportation/parking options for getting to and from the event?

 There will be parking in an adjacent field. 

Lodging

you're kind of on your own here! 

 

What can I bring into the event?

Bring a determination to finish and to finish well to The ROJR 2026.

 

Donations

For those who may be unable to make it to the event and would like to help the Grimm family out with a donation (or would just like to make a donation) please got to https://www.gofundme.com/jeremy-grimms-wife-and-kids

Event Description: The BOSSCROS5 p/b 545 VELO cyclocross race will be held at the Middlesex County 4H Fairground located just 20 miles from the I-95/Route 2 exchange. In addition to scintillating racing including the first ECCC collegiate race of the year, the grounds include ample parking and proper restrooms. Planned amenities include timing by Atwood Racing Services, a Kids Race, and a club/sponsor tent row.
Please note that the facility prohibits alcohol sales/consumption.

Course Description: The course will grace the field and tree section of the fairground, which traces its “Head, Heart, Hands, and Health” heritage back 60 years. The roughly one-and-a-quarter mile lap eschews elevation in favor of power sections, technical turns, planks, and a set of Belgian steps that only the best dare to ride. Staging will be by Crossresults.com ranking, then order of registration.

Registration: Registration is on BikeReg at https://www.bikereg.com/bosscross (online registration closes at 11:45am on Friday Oct 2). Racers may register for second and additional races at $15 each. Day-of registration is an additional $10. USAC one-day licenses can be purchased for $15. For on-site payments, 545 VELO accepts cash and PayPal but not Venmo.

Contact Information: Director and BikeReg Administration: Jeff Dieffenbach, deepbrook@gmail.com

Contact Info:  ECCC MTB Coordination Team, mtb@eccc-cycling.com

Collegiate fields are open only to full time collegiate students with valid USAC Collegiate licenses.  Open races are available for USAC non-collegiate riders with domestic USA Cycling licenses.  Jerseys and bibs for all collegiate riders must feature school names and/or logo, or be generic blank kits; non-scholastic club and trade team kits are not permitted.  USA Cycling licenses available for sale on-site.  Consult the ECCC website at https://eccc-cycling.com/ for more information on categories, eligibility, licensing, and other general questions.

Registration
Fees:  All Collegiate races $40; Team Relay $35/team

There is no prize money or merchandise offered at this event.

Pre-Registration is available on-line at BikeReg.com, where service charges might apply. USAC race fees include ECCC surcharge.  Registrations not received before 5pm on October 1st will incur a $5 per rider per event late fee. Large ECCC Teams may submit a spreadsheet with the following information: Rider Name, USAC License Number, Race Category and Races being entered for each rider. This spreadsheet must be sent to mtb@eccc-cycling.com and received by October 1st at 5pm in order to avoid a $5 late registration fee per rider per event.

Registration is located near parking area for all races. It opens at 7:30am and closes at 10:00 at the endurance venues, and opens at 11:00 and ends at 1:00 at the gravity venues.

Promoter is not required to refund pre-registration in an event of an unforeseen cancellation.

EventName: Women's Cycling Collective: Century Jubilee - 102/51/22mi Women's Gravel
EventNotes:
Women’s Cycling Collective: 

Century Jubilee

Date: Saturday, October 3rd

Start time: 7:45am

Location: Frost Beer Works, Hinesburg, Vermont

 

Come join a community of warm, endurance minded, bright spirited women riders for our second annual Century Jubilee: 100/50/22mi Women's Gravel as we ride through mixed surface roads in southern Chittenden and northern Addison County, starting and ending at Frost Beer Works, crafter of tropical, balanced, hazy IPAs and dedicated supporter of women in cycling.

 

Whether you're experienced with rides of longer duration or have been working to develop comfort and confidence as you build your capacity, there's opportunity here for you. Women's Cycling Collective is focused on offering collaborative, rider-focused events designed to support, encourage and connect women while they explore their potential through the context of the bike and the lens of endurance, training, and the natural world. We invite you to be part of the collective energy that serves to uplift, empower, and inspire women both on and off the bike.

 

Thank you to our generous business supporters and partners for enriching rider experience and making this event possible: Frost Beer Works, Velocio, Burlington Physical Therapy, Julbo, Darn Tough Vermont, Bivo, Bennett Creative Co. and Karen Mulkey Jewelry.

 

General Information: Details, including routes and other specifics are subject to change. All participants will be emailed updated and current information, including routes and course information, in the days leading up to the ride.

  • Full registrations for the 100-mile and 50-mile routes include ride, aid/SAG stops (mile 18, 42, 51, 60, 84, and102), access to personal drop bags and bins to discard layers and gear at each SAG, 2 raffle tickets, commemorative print (for the first 35 registered riders across all distances), Aromas of India meal, and a complimentary Frost Beer Works draught pour. Registration for the 22-mile route includes ride, aid/SAG stop (mile 13), access to personal drop bag and bin to discard layers and gear at SAG, raffle ticket, commemorative print (for the first 35 registered riders across all distances). Meal, served at 11:15am is sold separately for the 22-mile route.

    • There are a number of questions we are asking participants to answer during the registration process. While only some are “required,” responding to all will help us shape the event in ways that better meet individual needs and preferences when and where possible.

    • We ask that you identify with pronouns she or they if you choose to register for any of the Century Jubilee offerings.

    • Registration closes Sunday, September 27th at 9pm. There is NO DAY OF EVENT REGISTRATION.

 

  • Limited number of complimentary commemorative Century Jubilee 8x10" posters:

    • Hand printed and numbered locally at New Duds.

    • Offered to the first 35 registered participants.

 

  • Complimentary Century Jubilee t-shirt for riders who register before Wednesday, September 23rd!

    • Designed and by Stephanie Bennett at Bennett Creative.

    • Sweatshirts available in lieu of t-shirts.

 

  • The route consists of one clockwise 51mi loop that is repeated in reverse (counterclockwise) for the 102mi participants.

    • For women completing the 102, this will provide a sense of familiarity in the second half, with a different perspective and feel since riding in the opposite direction.

    • Since our personal paces vary, many women will have crossover as they complete the first fifty miles and/or continue for a second lap as they work towards one hundred, promoting a sense of togetherness, an opportunity to cheer each other along, or simply share a smile or wave in recognition of our shared experience.

    • The route will be partially marked. Riders are expected to carry bike computers/GPS/phones that can support navigation.

FOR 100 and 50-mile routes:

  • Support and resupply at aid stations and with local business partners is available every 9-25 miles. (Check in at all aid stations along respective routes is required of all participants.) Sunrise is at 7:00am and sunset is at 6:40pm.

    • Mile 0 (start): Frost Beer Works, Hinesburg, VT

    • Mile 18.1: Burlington Physical Therapy tent on Hardscrabble Road - full SAG (nutrition, hydration), drop bag access, and portable restroom

    • Mile 42: Adam's Berry Farm, Charlotte, VT: partial SAG (popsicle provided by Adam's Berry Farm, water) drop bag access, farm stand open for purchases

    • Mile 51: Frost Beer Works, Hinesburg, VT - full SAG (nutrition, hydration), drop bag access, restroom, access to parked vehicles (also local amenities such as gas station, grocery, convenience store, coffee shop, etc. nearby)

      • 50mi riders: Aroma's finisher meal (lunch delivered between 11:15-11:30am), Frost Beer Works draught pour

      • 100mi riders: full SAG (nutrition, hydration) drop bag access and restroom

        • cut off departure time for 100mi riders = 12:45pm

    • Mile 60: Adam's Berry Farm, Charlotte, VT: partial SAG (popsicle provided by Adam's Berry Farm, water) drop bag access, farm stand open for purchases

      • cut off departure time for 100mi riders = 1:45pm

    • Mile 84: Burlington Physical Therapy tent on Hardscrabble Road - full SAG (nutrition, hydration), drop bag access and portable restroom

      • cut off departure time for 100mi riders = 4:00pm

    • Mile 102: Frost Beer Works, Hinesburg, VT

      • all 100mi riders expected to return to Frost Beer Works by sunset at 6:40pm

      • 100mi riders: Aroma's finisher meal, Frost Beer Works draught pour

  • Option to access or discard personal gear and supplies along the way.

    • 100- and 50- mile riders may choose to prepare personal drop bags labeled with their name and the SAG stop they wish to have it accessible (miles 18/87 - Burlington Physical Therapy tent on Hardscrabble Road, miles 43/62 - Adam's Berry Farm, mile 50 - Frost Beer Works)

    • Bins to drop unneeded layers or gear will be available at all SAG.

    • The drop bags and bins will be brought back to Frost Beer Works by 6:00pm. If riders have left the venue before then, arrangements can be made to pick up gear in the future.

FOR 22-mile route:

  • Support and resupply at aid station is available at mile 13. (Check in at aid station is required of all participants.)

    • Mile 0 (start): Frost Beer Works, Hinesburg, VT

    • Mile 13: Adam's Berry Farm, Charlotte, VT: partial SAG (popsicle provided by Adam's Berry Farm, water) drop bag access, farm stand open for purchases

    • Mile 22: Frost Beer Works, Hinesburg, VT - full SAG (nutrition, hydration), drop bag access, restroom, access to parked vehicles (also local amenities such as gas station, grocery, convenience store, coffee shop, etc. nearby)

       

  • Option to access or discard personal gear and supplies along the way.

    • 22-mile riders may choose to prepare personal drop bag labeled with their name and the SAG stop they wish to have it accessible at mile 13 - Adam's Berry Farm.

    • A bin to drop unneeded layers or gear will be available at SAG.

    • The drop bags and bins will be brought back to Frost Beer Works by 6:00pm. If riders have left the venue before then, arrangements can be made to pick up gear in the future.

Route links in blue (revised 9/22/26): Complete routes include checking in at every aid station.

  • 100mi (103.3mi - 2 laps, clockwise, then counterclockwise) - WCC Century Jubilee 100 - 2026

  • 50mi (52.5mi - 1 lap, clockwise) - WCC Century Jubilee 50 - 2026

  • 22mi (22mi - clockwise - cutoff from 50- and 100-mile routes at Rotax Road) - WCC Century Jubilee 22 - 2026

Cut off times: 

  • All 100mi riders must depart from Frost Beer Works for 2nd lap by 12:45pm

  • All 100mi riders must depart from Mile 60 Adam's Berry Farm SAG/Aid Station by 1:45pm

  • All 100mi riders must depart from Mile 84 BPT/Hardscrabble SAG/Aid Station by 4:00pm

  • All 22mi riders expected back at Frost Beer Works by 11:00am

  • All 50mi riders expected back at Frost Beer Works by 3pm

  • All 100mi riders expected back at Frost Beer Works by 6:40pm

 

Packet pick-up, SAG personal drop bag drop-off:

    • raffle at 6:45pm includes Darn Tough Socks and Julbo lifestyle glasses

    • must be present to win

  • Saturday, October 3rd, Frost Beer Works, 6:50-7:20am

 

Raffle items: 

(2 tickets included with each 100- and 50-mile registration, and 1 ticket included with each 22-mile registration, limit one raffle item per participant)

  • Velocio - 3 x Shoulder Season Bundles (each bundle includes arm warmer, leg warmer, merino beanie, and rain shoe cover)

  • Julbo - 5 x pairs of Performance Glasses, 1 x pair Lifestyle Glasses

  • Women's Cycling Collective - (2) 1mo. live virtual winter training WCC Velocity Basic Membership (or prorated 1mo discount if athlete is purchasing full season membership package)

Full schedule of events:

  • Friday, October 2nd

    • 5:00-7:00pm - Packet/bib/t-shirt pick up/drop bag collection at Frost Beer Works

  • Saturday, October 3rd

    • 6:50 - 7:20am (sunrise at 7am) - Packet/bib/t-shirt pick up/drop bag collection at Frost Beer Works

      • PLEASE NOTE: Riders arriving later than 7:20am may need to wait until 8:20am when volunteers return after the neutral rollout to pick up their packets and begin their ride.

    • 7:30am - gather to connect with fellow riders and for group photo

    • 7:35am - official group welcome, safety review, reminders, remaining questions and answers

    • 7:45am - 2.7mi neutral rollout led by Women's Cycling Collective to Lily Bud Farm on Baldwin Road

    • ~8:05am - all waves arrive for regroup at Lily Bud Farm

      • bin available to discard unwanted layers after warming up

      • water jug available to top off bottles

      • one more group photo, reminders, official ride start

    • 11:00am - All 22mi riders expected to be back at Frost Beer Works

    • 11:15/30am - lunch begins - first delivery of Aromas of India finishers meals

    • 12:45pm - Cut off time for 100mi. riders departing from mile 51, Frost Beer Works

    • 1:45pm - Cut off time for 100mi. riders departing from mile 60, Adam's Berry Farm

    • 3:00pm - All 50mi riders expected to be back at Frost Beer Works

    • 4:30pm - Cut off time for 100mi. riders departing from mile 84, BPT/Hardscrabble Road

    • 6:40pm (sunset) - All 100mi riders expected to be back at Frost Beer Works

    • Raffle drawing time TBD - riders do not need to be present to win, arrangements will be made to pick up items at alternate time or postage can be paid if winners wish to have item shipped.

 

Pre-event Workshops, Clinics, and Coaching:

 

 

Additional pre-event workshops, clinics, and coaching are available on an individual or small group basis. Please contact organizer and coach, Liz Wolf, if interested.

 

Barring more extreme, rare or dangerous weather conditions, this event and associated offerings will take place. If we need to cancel Saturday’s ride due to extreme or dangerous weather, we will make every effort to reschedule it for Sunday, October 4th. Please keep this possibility in mind when making plans for the weekend of the ride. In the unforeseen event of cancelation or reschedule, refunds will not be issued.

If you have questions about event details, any of the offerings, or want/need to learn more before making a decision to participate, please do not hesitate to reach out to Liz Wolf, Century Jubilee Director.

EventName: RISE: Ride. Celebrate. Take Care of You
EventNotes:
RISE: Ride for more. More adventure. More community. More awareness.

Women of OZ Annual Fundraiser

WHY WE RISE

All year long, Women of OZ gives back to women in our community through free rides, skills clinics, education, mentorship, and connection.

We believe more women belong on bikes—and that cost should never be what keeps someone from finding her people, building confidence, or discovering what she’s capable of.

ONCE A YEAR, WE RISE.

Join us for our annual fundraiser in partnership with the Breast Cancer Foundation of the Ozarks (BCFO).

This is our day to:

Ride together | Rally around women in our community |Raise awareness for breast health |Fund the free programming that happens all year long

YOUR TICKET INCLUDES

Guided Experience - choose from MTB Ride, Gravel Ride, Art Ride or Yoga
Eat good food
Enjoy a bevvie
Dance to music
Hear from an inspiring woman
Connect with your community

BONUS IMPACT

Through our partnership with BCFO, every guest receives a confidential mammogram voucher — yours to use or pass along to a woman who needs it.

 

COME FOR THE RIDE. STAY FOR THE PARTY.

Leave knowing you helped create more access, more opportunity, and more community for women in the Ozarks.

Because when women show up for women, good things happen.

 

ONE RIDE. ONE CELEBRATION. A WHOLE YEAR OF IMPACT.

 

Ride Experience Details:

We will have ride leaders for skill levels between Beginner to Advanced. 

If you're new to mountain biking OR have never done a fundamentals skills clinic we REQUIRE YOU to start with the WOZ Fundamental Skills Clinic during registration. Regardless of your riding experience we feel taking this skills course from one of our WOZ certified instructors will help improve your riding and create a better riding experience for all.

What do you need to attend the Flagship?  A mountain bike in good working order (contact a local bike shop for a tune up), helmet, closed toe athletic shoes, flat repair kit, water and snacks.  We also recommend sunglasses for eye protection and gloves.

***Ride levels are based on YOUR CURRENT skills and endurance levels *** We want everyone to have the best and safest experience possible so we’ve laid out a “rating” system to help align you with the right ride group. Please review the skills, endurance, milage and proposed trails.  Being in the right group makes a better ride for all. 

At registration first choose your riding and fitness level, then choose the best description among the groups. Remember if you want to ride with a friend, register ASAP in the same Level AND Group # to ensure you'll be in the same group.  

Choose your group:

FUNDAMENTAL SKILLS CLINIC... this is the starting place
Select this group if you have never ridden a mountain bike,  it’s been a little longer than you would like to admit, OR you've never taken this clinic before….. Welcome!   You have to start somewhere and this is the place!  Even the most advanced riders need to brush up on these essential skills.  This Skills Clinic will cover the fundamental of mountain biking and then you'll hit the trail for a 2-3 mile ride. 

Skill Level 1 

Skills you can perform:
Staying upright while pedaling
Fitness Level- no requirement 

GREEN ….New
You’ve ridden on the dirt multiple times now and you are starting to get the hang of things. You are now putting those skills from the clinic into play and working on shifting, braking, and body position.  Ride 5-7 miles.
Skills you can perform:
Skill level 1+
Level pedals while riding 
Riding with one finger over L & R brake levers
Getting to know berms (those are those turns with the dirt) 
Fitness Level 1 
Able to ride 30 minutes on easy terrain
Climbing a hill on the bike might require a breather break on the way up, and at the top of the hill. (I thought hills were for going down??)

GREEN +.... New with constant improvement 
Here to add the obstacles and steeper hills, but you are taking fewer breaks and pushing the ride time and mileage.  You are attempting more rocky surfaces, bridges and to roll over roots. (Yep we just roll right over those suckers.) Distances up to 8 miles or 2 hours are doable. Down Tristan’s?  Let go up it! Ride 5-7 miles.
Skills you can perform:
Skill level 2+
Standing on level pedals in “ready” position comfortably
Getting comfortable with appropriate gear shifting 
Novice on cornering and berms 
Comfortable crossing bridges 
Okay rolling over low roots/rocks and through tight trees  
Fitness Level Required 2 
You ride 2x a week
You can handle non-stop riding for up to an hour on easy terrain, after that it’s hit or miss.
You can climb up Crystal Bridges hill without stopping, but give me a breather at the top!

BLUE ....Confident and Fit.... attempting rock gardens
The rides are getting longer and the pace quicker.  Getting quicker out of berms you are confident in shifting, comfortable on single track and open to attempting obstacles.  You’re getting the hang of Coler, riding most of Slaughter Pen, and may have ridden Back 40 or at least parts of it. Ride 9-12 miles.
Skills you can perform:
Skill Level 3+
Controlled braking
Must be comfortable cornering and with berms 
Bike-body separation are natural
Comfortable with most moderate terrain (steeper, rockier, wetter, etc.)
Confident with wide switchbacks
Able to look up the trail and anticipate shifting, position change, obstacles, etc.
Fitness Level 3 
You ride 2-3x a week on an average in season week
You can climb longer with soft pedaling as a recovery instead of stopping
You can ride moderate pace for 2 hours with minimal stops 
Must be able to climb Ozone 
Intermediate skill group: here because you’re still working on upping the mileage and ride time. 15 miles or 3 hours might be my cutoff!                 
                              
BLUE +... Confident, fit and ready for a 3hr ride
You’ve been riding for awhile now, put a lot of time and mileage in to riding confidently and tackling bigger challenges are a regular thing. You are comfortable with fast descents, rock gardens, more technical climbs and features.  Ride 10-15 miles. 
Skills you can perform: 
Skill Level 4+ Confident with bike handling skills with roots, rocks, tight corners, etc
Your tires are leaving the ground
Climbing technical terrain 
Comfortable in tight Berms/Switchbacks and exit with acceleration 
Can ride technical single track 
Able to get up and over moderate obstacles up to 6 inches off ground
Fitness Level 4 
Riding 3-4x a week 
3  hour rides are doable
Able to climb continuously without breaks 
Can ride most of Back 40 

BLACK....Advanced rider and can ride with a pro-mtb'r
Ride now, talk later.  You are up for fast paced, intense, challenging, demanding, some good ol light-hearted competition!  Be ready to ride fast, nail some jumps and drops, and possibly get a QOM in the meantime! Ride 15+ miles.
Skills you can perform:
Skill Level 5+
Comfortable with drops and changing technical terrain 
Hop over obstacles  
Able to perform front wheel/rear wheel lifts (up to 6 inches as needed) 
Fitness Level 5  
Riding 4-5x a week 
Considers racing around the Back 40 in around 3hrs FUN
Ready to move at a rapid pace throughout ride
Continuous movement, breaks only to refuel 
Can ride Rock Solid and Schroen Train

EventNotes:
This November, Backyard Bikepacking DFW is hosting our fourth “Intro to Bikepacking” event. This will be a great opportunity to try out bikepacking without the hassle of planning a route, finding a crew, or leaving your backyard. If this sounds like your kind of fun, don't wait - this event has sold out in the past!

We will be heading from Weatherford, TX to Lake Mineral Wells SP (50 mile round trip) and camping overnight. Once at the campsite, there will be opportunities for swimming, hiking, fishing, and birdwatching. It's sure to be a great time!

"Just Another Dirty Dozen" is back for it's 9th year.   This is a bicycle ride up the 13 toughest hills in (and around) Wheeling. Just like the Pittsburgh dirty dozen will be keeping points for the top 5 finishers of each hill. It will be a neutral slower paced ride in between hills. Drew Hollis will blow a whistle at the bottom of each hill indicating the start of the race for each hill. A scorekeeper will be keeping score at the top of each hill. Please call out your name as you pass the top of the hill.

Ride will be lightly supported. Helmet required.  Lights Recommended. THIS IS A DIFFICULT AND CHALLENGING ROAD RIDE WITH STEEP CLIMBS AND DESCENTS. RIDE AT YOUR OWN RISK!

The Route is approximately 45miles with +6,500' of climb. The ride should take around 5 hours because of the slow pace between hills and waiting for the rest of the group at the top of each hill.

We will be leaving from the Wheelcraft parking lot (2187 National Rd Wheeling, WV 26003) at 9:00am.  This is the first year we are having the ride on a Satuday.

EventNotes:
Pump Track Time Trial

We're excited to open the Township's Pump Track to residents and riders from around the area for a chance to see how fast they can get around the course.

We'll offer an Expert Line, which includes the track's jump line, and Line A, which uses only the rollers and banked turns.  We will also have use the short circle track for our beginners and strider riders.  

The challenge: how quickly can you get around the track without pedaling? Riders may take a couple of pedal strokes to drop into the track, but once you cross the start timing line, no more pedaling is allowed.

For complete rules, please visit our website.

Parking
Please park in the lot by the Pump Track. Once that lot is full, please park at the Hanover Township Community Center, 3630 Jacksonville Road, Bethlehem, PA 19017. From the Community Center parking lot, follow the trail past the playground and dog park — it's a short walk that leads right to the pump track.

Food
This event will not have food or food trucks available for purchase. We'll provide water for participants. Please bring your own food and drinks for both participants and spectators.

About 

Join us for the final Prospect Park race of the year in honor of Al Toefield (Kissena Cycling Club founder) and Pete Senia (legendary race official and NYC racing influencer).

Registration 

  • Please register online. There may be Day of reg allowed if there is space.
  • Register online early! The field limits are strictly enforced and most fields have filled up in the past.
  • If you have a chip from CRCA, Prospect Park, etc please use it. It will help speed up the results.
  • You will receive a new bib for this race. No need to use your series number from 2026.
  • Masters, Women, and Juniors race with their category.  Junior entry fee is $10. Women entry fee is $25. Juniors/Women: Juniors use code PPJunior26 and Women/NB use PPWomen26 to receive your discount. If you don't fall into one of these categories, don't use the code.
  • For those without a USA Cycling Racing license ONE-DAY LICENSES are available on Bikereg for $15 .  Please note that one-day licenses can be purchased only by unlicensed or Category 5 Men or unlicensed or Category 4 women.
  • Race day number pickup opens at 5:40am and closes at 6:30am. There are no refunds or credits if you arrive late.

Start/Finish Location

The Start/Finish and registration area is located at the 3rd Street entrance at Prospect Park West.  This is the same location we use every year, about a 1/4 mile past the main hill and Grand Army Plaza.

Prizes

  • Cat 1-2-3 = $500 all cash prize list. 7 places.
  • Cat 3-4 = $200 to top 3 places
  • Cat 5/Novice = Medals. 5 places.

Disclaimer

  • Promoter reserves the right to shorten race distances due to weather conditions and/or time constraints.
  • Promoter reserves the right to cancel, combine fields and/or reduce prize money if minimum fields are not met.

Course Description

3.4 mile loop along the park roadway in Prospect Park. The course features one moderate (big ring) hill and sweeping turns. Although the course is closed to traffic, you will frequently encounter other park users (pedestrians, cyclist etc.), on the park roadway. For this reason all competitors are advised to stay alert and be polite to other park users. 

VERY IMPORTANT - PLEASE READ!

Riders must not enter the "recreation" lane (aka jogger's lane, including the buffer zone) on the left side of the roadway on the west side for any reason.  Riders must not enter EITHER recreation lane(aka jogger's lane, including the buffer zone) on the east side of the park. Any rider entering this lane, even momentarily, will be disqualified and will not be permitted to race in NY Parks for three months and will not be permitted to race in any Kissena Cycling Club event in Prospect Park for one year.

This is a unique opportunity to experience a historic discipline in a welcoming and supportive environment.

EventNotes:
TIME & LOCATION
October 3-4, 2026

Jarrod's Place Bike Park
1234 Dirt Road
Summerville, GA 30747
United States

Located in Summerville, just 90 minutes north of Atlanta, Jarrod’s Place is an off-road oasis for mountain bikers who crave an adrenaline-fueled experience. The park is surrounded by dense woods and rocky hills, making it the perfect venue for a high-intensity championship event. The challenging terrain is designed to push racers to their absolute limit — fast, technical, and wild.

DESCRIPTION
The Championship Finale course at Jarrod's Place is brutal and built to decide champions. It’s a mix of everything that makes enduro racing thrilling: steep, technical climbs, high-speed descents, challenging rock gardens, and some serious downhill bangers that will make riders feel the full force of the season’s grind. It’s do or die for the series standings.

Jarrod’s Place Bike Park is known for its world-class trails and raw, natural terrain — designed to challenge even the most skilled riders. With its technical rock features, intense climbs, and high-speed descents, it’s the perfect place for an all-or-nothing finale.

The park is built for riders who want to test their limits — and the championship finale at this venue will be the ultimate test of endurance, skill, and bravery. Racers will go head-to-head on some of the most gnarly terrain in the country, with nothing but pride, glory, and the title of Go Nuts Biking International Enduro Champion on the line.

15. All protest must be filed within 20 minutes of the last competitor completing the final race stage of the day. 
16. If you encounter an injured/downed rider, please stop and check on them. If a rider is seriously injured or unconscious, let officials know immediately or call 911.

Go Nuts International Enduro Series eMTB Rules as follows: 

1) Maximum 750watts - assistance up to 20 miles per hour - Pedaling assistance only. No hand or foot throttle allowed. Automatic disqualification. Bicycles must remain locked, i.e., no modification of wheel sensor from factory circumference or any other modification to manipulate the factory set speed of the bike.

2) Throttle mechanisms are prohibited.

3) Studded tires are prohibited.

4) It is forbidden to change e-bike during the event even if the rider finishes the event with the same race plate.

5) Technical assistance consists of the replacement or repairs of any part of the e-bike at the exception of the frame, wheels or battery.

6) Races will be conducted regardless of weather conditions.  In the event of rain or other unfavorable conditions, it may be necessary to alter the order of the event schedule, including but not limited to, adjusting the length of the race or delaying or stopping the program completely.  Should a delay occur, every effort will be made to resume the schedule in a timely fashion if conditions significantly improve.

7) No headphones, earphones or sound devices permitted. Horns and bells are permitted.

8) Riders are required to wear the appropriate helmet. Other protective gear is optional; gloves, goggles, elbow/knee guards, etc.

9) Shirt, shoes, and pants/shorts required. Clipless or flat pedals are both permitted.

10) An E-Mountain Bike is a bike operated with two energy sources, human pedal power and an electric engine, which only provides assistance when the rider is pedaling.

11) Any behavior deemed inappropriate or unsportsmanlike like conduct will not be tolerated. Verbal or physical infractions will result in a disqualification. 

Severe weather policy
Unless otherwise posted, race will be held. Safety of all racers is our main priority. If there is a delay or cancellation due to weather conditions, racers are responsible for checking information posted by director. The information will be posted on the homepage of website, social network avenues, and via email up to 72 hours prior to the race.

Transfer/Refund Policy
There will be no registration refunds once registration is processed. We will allow transfers to upcoming races. All transfers must be requested 10 days prior and is only allowed for races that were rescheduled. Transfers will not be allowed 10 days before race or after race.
