KING'S TOUR OF THE QUABBIN – Sunday, Oct. 4, 2026 – Hardwick, Mass.

NEW THIS YEAR! Early Bird registration fees ($40/$60) apply until 9 p.m. July 3. After that, registration costs $10 more.

Online registration closes at 9 p.m. Sept. 30. Fees go up another $10 for day-of-ride registration.

PLEASE NOTE: Due to low registration for the metric century, there has been a route change. The link has been updated below.

Bicycle around the Quabbin Reservoir, a pristine jewel in the heart of Massachusetts. Choose from two road routes (64 or 101 miles) or two gravel routes (approximately 44 or 77 miles, each approximately half paved). Not much traffic; plenty of hills.

Start/finish for all routes is at Hardwick Winery, 3305 Greenwich Road, Hardwick, MA 01082. Check-in opens at 6:45 a.m. Start times are flexible, but we recommend century riders and gravel riders start 7:00-8:00 a.m., and road metric riders start 8:00-9:00 a.m. All routes except the Road Metric will stop at Petersham Common.

Routes will not be arrowed. Routes will be scouted prior to the event for road/trail conditions and may be modified accordingly. Final Ride with GPS links will be emailed to online registrants the week before the ride.

Road metric (64 miles, approx. 4900 feet of climbing)
https://ridewithgps.com/routes/42382528
Rest stops at mile 28 (Pelham, 8:30 a.m.-11 a.m.) and mile 48 (Petersham Common, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.).

Road century (101 miles, 6000+ feet of climbing)
https://ridewithgps.com/routes/42382603

Rest stops at mile 28 (Rt. 202 in Pelham, 8:30-11 a.m.), mile 58 (Leverett Co-op store), and mile 85 (Petersham Common, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.). Road century riders get a $5 credit to use at the Leverett store.

 

Gravel Loop (77 miles, approx. 6000 feet of climbing)
https://ridewithgps.com/routes/47076480

Rest stops at mile 28 (Petersham Common, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.) and mile 60 (Petersham Common again).

 

Little Gravel – hard finish (45 miles, approx.3400 feet of climbing)
https://ridewithgps.com/routes/54352597

Rest stop at mile 29 (Petersham Common, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.)

 

Little Gravel – easy finish (43 miles, approx. 3100 feet of climbing)
https://ridewithgps.com/routes/54352606

Rest stop at mile 29 (Petersham Common, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m.)
 

The gravel routes avoid DCR trails. On the Little Gravel route, there's an option at mile 40 to do an easy finish (remainder of route is mostly paved, and the route totals 43 miles) or a hard finish (remainder of route is unpaved, with nearly 300 feet more climbing, and the route totals 45 miles).

Not sure which route is for you? Not to worry -- you can change your selection online at any time before registration closes. You can even wait until ride day and decide in the middle of the ride. Both road routes are the same until the Quabbin Visitor Center, at mile 18. Both gravel routes go to the Petersham rest stop at mile 28. So whether you're on the road or the gravel, you can decide partway how to continue.

Limited to 150 riders.

Refreshments afterwards at Hardwick Winery, with a food truck for the afternoon.

More info: https://sevenhillswheelmen.org/kings-tour-of-the-quabbin/

ANNUAL WALNUT VALLEY METRIC

The Walnut Valley Metric routes travel through scenic Cowley County on gently rolling hills and lightly traveled secondary roads. Registration includes SAGs and lunch at Liberty Township School House.  The gravel route does include two "stone arch bridges" and two that you can ride to 1/3 of a mile from the route.  Several additional "stone arch bridges" are within .5 to .75 m on gravel from the 65 m road route.  There are only 1700 stone arch bridges remaining in the United States according to Cowley County website.  Interestingly, 18 of those historical stone bridges are in Cowley County!

Proceeds from the ride benefit the Prairie Sunset Trail and Redbud Trail.

NOTE: online t-shirt orders end 9/24/26. Limited t-shirts will be available for purchase day of, and orders will be taken at registration if your size is not available.

Or check out all three! https://ridewithgps.com/events/66226-walnut-valley-metric-2018 

Rest Stops and SAGS

Rest stops will be approximately 15-17 miles apart. Water, fruit, cookies and other snacks will be offered. Restrooms will be available at SAG stops. SAG vehicles with water and mechanical assistance will run the routes. Riders unable to finish will be transported back to Winfield Recreation Center. Lunch will be available for all riders, starting at 10:00 AM.

Thanks to Jimmy John's for helping provide food for lunch and SAG stops.

Your Health & Safety

Be sure your bicycle is in good working order. Arrive early the day of the ride to check your bike and tires.

Other things to remember:

  • No headphones or ear buds: you need to hear and be aware of those around you.
  • Carry a tire pump and patch kit.
  • Fluid intake is very important: Remember to carry water bottles on your bike.
  • Eat before you are hungry and drink before you are thirsty.
  • Cyclists should ride not more than two abreast and should not impede the flow of traffic.
  • Stop for stop signs and red lights.
  • Cross railroad tracks at a right angle to prevent damage to your bike and possible injury to you. In wet weather, cyclists are encouraged to dismount and walk their bikes across the tracks.

All riders must observe traffic laws.

Note: This ride is rain or shine. 

In the event of cancellation, no refunds will be offered as it is a benefit for local rail trails.

E-BIKE REGULATIONS (THIS IS A WORK IN PROGRESS....LEARNING AS WE GO....)
As we continue to provide e-bike racing in the Month of Mud series we want it to be a safe but welcoming racing environment for all mountain bike enthusiasts and racers. In order to do so we believe the following standards are fair for our local grassroots series.
• E- Bikes that are USAC UCI or GNCC certified are legal.
• E-Bikes must pedal assist with a max speed of 20mph.
• Programmable E-Bikes must be set and locked to 750 watts and 20 MPH. • Throttle mechanisms are prohibited. • Boost buttons must be removed or disabled. • No aftermarket modifications will be allowed.
• E-Bikes must be inspected 30 minutes before the race start. • E-Bikes MUST be in the off position at the starting line and powered up at the official's instructions. • Settings must be verified immediately after finishing. • Any E-Bike that is found to be illegal, rider will forfeit all prizes and points and will be suspended for remaining races. All categories. • Officials carry the right to test any E-Bike in question. Month of mud is not liable for any damage that may occur during testing. If you withhold your E-Bike to this test, you will be disqualified from the race.
• Passing etiquette must be followed. Unsportsmanlike behavior, foul riding, use of profanity, or flagrant discourtesy directed at participants, spectators, or officials will result in disqualification.
• Analog bikes have the right of way, you must yield to a racer in a different class to pass you when appropriate and safe to do so.
• No battery swapping during the race
 
OTHER NOTES:
· Helmets are required for all races.
· Please arrive early to check in. Check-in closes 30 minutes prior to start times.

Sioux Falls Bike Racing Great Bear Enduro
Great Bear Ski Valley | Sioux Falls, SD
Sunday, October 4

Get ready to race one of Sioux Falls’ most unique mountain bike events! The Great Bear Enduro is bringing enduro-style racing to Great Bear Ski Valley with 5 timed stages featuring the hills, trails, descents, and terrain that make Great Bear such a fun place to ride.

If you've never raced an enduro before, the format is simple: only the designated stages are timed. Riders pedal between stages at their own pace, giving you a chance to recover, catch up with friends, and get ready to send the next one. Your times from all 5 stages are combined to determine your overall finishing time.

Expect a mix of fast descents, technical trail, punchy sections, and plenty of opportunities to test your bike-handling skills. You don't need to be a downhill racer to join in—the enduro format makes this an awesome event for experienced racers and first-time competitors alike.

5 Timed Stages
Untimed transfers between stages
Lowest combined stage time wins
Prizes
Food & beverages available for purchase
Loads of fun

Check-in: 8:00–9:00 AM
Rider Meeting: 9:00–9:15 AM
Race Opens: 9:30 AM
Race Closes: 12:30 PM
Podiums: 1:00 PM

Following the rider meeting, we ask that riders head out in race order to help keep traffic flowing smoothly between stages.

And we're saving something special for the finish: Stage 5 will bring riders all the way down to the finish directly in front of the Great Bear Ski Chalet, making it the perfect spot for friends, family, and spectators to watch the final runs and cheer racers home.

Bring your mountain bike, your friends, and your willingness to go fast. Whether you're chasing the podium or just looking for an awesome day of riding and racing, the Great Bear Enduro is about competition, community, and having a ridiculously good time on bikes.

Chief Tecumseh

OMBC Series #10
Annie's Race
 
Sunday, October 4, 2026, at High NOON 
 
Annie's Race: Annie Rooney was integral in the development of the Tecumseh's Revenge race and an avid OMBC Series Racer. Tragically, she was struck by a drunk driver who took her life. In 2017, "Annie's Law" became signed into law to help prevent similar tragedies from occurring. For everyone who was privileged to have known her, Annie's warm smile, enthusiasm for life and all things mountain biking inspired us. At Scioto Trails, we celebrate her life and the race she brought to the OMBC Race Series.
 
2016 Revenge Race Report by Quickdirt
 
REGISTRATION WILL OPEN SOON
RACE INFO:  The race will begin and end at the Ross Shelter located along the park road. Follow race parking signs.  
 
Race Description:
Tecumseh's Revenge is entering its ninth year with the Ohio Series. It will continue to be Fast and Furious. Not to be confused with the botched US Government Operation that put hundreds of guns in the hands of criminals, THIS Fast and Furious will entice you with newly built single track trail, with more to come including speedy down hills before hitting you with a reality check as Tecumseh unleashes his mighty fury in the form of lung busting climbs.
 
TRAIL DESCRIPTION:  The course is not technical, but has some steep climbs and descents.  The race will start and end at the Ross Shelter on Stoney Creek Road. Racers will head east on Stoney Creek Road and turn right on fire road 5. At the top of the climb racers will head left at the fork and take the first trail on the left (Estep Hollow) everyone will go right at the trail split on lap 1 which will eventually take you to fire road 5, turn right and proceed past the road closed gates. Racers will then descend the South Ridge trail on the left and follow it to Wilson Run Road (turn right) turn right on fire road 7 stay right at the split, left on Estep Hollow trail. Novice riders will go left at the trail split to the finish. Sport and expert will stay right for laps 2 and 3.
 
Who was Tecumseh and why should I fear his revenge?
From: http://www.pc.gc.ca/lhn-nhs/on/fortgeorge/edu/edua3.aspx
Tecumseh was born in 1768 and was a Shawnee warrior chief who with his brother, the Prophet (Tenskwatawa), attempted to stop the advance of white settlement into the Old Northwest. Tecumseh believed that Indians must return to traditional ways, that they must forget intertribal rivalries and confederate, and that individual tribes must not sell land that all Indians held in common. In 1809 tribes in the Indiana Territory ceded much of their land to the United States. Tecumseh protested in vain to Governor William Henry Harrison. In the fall of 1811 he determined to carry his message to the Chickasaw, Choctaw, and Creek, He went south, leaving his
brother in charge at Prophet's Town, near Tippecanoe Creek, a utopian village where the Indians were to practice Tecumseh's principles. Before going, Tecumseh warned his brother not to attack Harrison's nearby forces. The Prophet ignored the warning and attacked. The Battle of Tippecanoe was not a clear cut American victory, but Prophet's Town was destroyed and Indian resistance
broken. After Tecumseh's return, he joined the British against the Americans in the War of 1812. His support for Isaac Brock at the capture of Detroit was decisive. Before the British approach, Tecumseh's warriors showed themselves in a never-ending line to the Americans. The warriors at the head of the line doubled back to join the end of the line and it appeared to General Hull that he was besieged by a massive force of Indians. This manoeuvre convinced Hull to surrender to avoid a massacre. As a brigadier general,
Tecumseh led over 2,000 warriors. He fought at the sieges of Fort Meigs, and Fort Stephenson, and his last battle was the Battle of the Thames at Chatham Ontario, where, clothed in traditional Indian deerskin garments, he was killed leading his warriors in a final stand against the invading Americans.
 
Will your team make a stand?
No Whiners allowed! For Tecumseh will have HIS revenge this day!

EventNotes:
We are so excited for your child to participate in NICA Discovery! 

 

All NICA Discovery adult leaders are background checked and hold a coaching license from NICA.  There will always be at least 2 leaders who have current first aid training. 

 

New Friends is the introductory level and is aimed at children who are new to biking but have some limited experience with neighborhood or urban riding.  These are children who can already balance and pedal a bike, but may have never ventured “off road.” Games and activities work on learning to better ride and operate a bike preparation for later buildable skills, and increasing stamina. 

 

Participants must be able to ride a bike without training wheels before joining a program and must be in 7-11 years old by program start date.

 

NICA Discovery Moundsville, WV meets Mondays at Grand Vue Park at 5:30-7:00 pm.

August 24

August 31

September 14

September 21

September 28

October 5

 

Required Documentation

ONLINE: 

  • Registration for NICA Discovery is through the platform BikeReg.  Go to bikereg.com and search “NICA Discovery” to find your location. 

IN PERSON: 

  • Parents must print, review this CODE OF CONDUCT with their child, sign and bring it to the first session for their child to participate. 
  • Every rider is also required to have a waiver and medical release form signed on file with NICA.  A link to the waiver may be found HERE.  Parents are asked to show confirmation that the online waiver has been signed before their child participates. 

Required Equipment

  • Helmet - Helmets should be less than 5 years old with no visible cracks or defects and fit your child’s head well without moving around while they ride. 
  • Footwear - Closed-toe (non-Croc like) shoes that fastened by laces, straps or buckles
  • Bike - Bike with knobby tires, gears, and two hand brakes. Bike tires should be no smaller than 20 inches.
  • Bike repair items - A replacement tube that fits your child’s tire. (dropped off at day one check in and returned at close of program if they are un-used.
  • Snug fitting small backpack  - Kids need to be able to carry water and snacks with them at all times.
  • Snacks/Hydration - Kids should always bring a snack and hydration with them to Discovery. 
    • Examples could include a granola bar, fruit snacks, or something that can easily be stored in a pocket or pack.
    • Hydration should consist of non caffeinated sports drinks or just good ole water! 

Recommended Equipment

  • Gloves - full-finger gloves to protect hands from abrasions in the case of a fall
  • Eye protection - generic sports glasses to protect from dust and debris (and bugs) kicked up while riding
  • Windbreaker /rain jacket/coat - weather conditions change throughout the season, your child should be prepared to ride in the conditions that are present on the day. Sessions will be altered or canceled if the weather conditions are unsafe. 
  • Athletic /Cycling pants- Loose fitting athletic pants. Cycling specific shorts are not required but some kids may be more comfortable.

What to Expect

Each lesson is broken down into 3 sections.  

  • Opener activities and objective/expectation setting
  • Skills activities and Games 
  • Wrap up and Reflection

There will be a  break mid-lesson for snacking/hydrating and general check in.

Each lesson builds on skills learned in the previous one.  To get the MOST out of NICA Discovery make sure your child can attend every lesson! 

For New Friends, the lessons consist of riding and playing in a park-like setting and are not trail dependent. Students will ride within that open space rather than out on trails, staying close to restroom facilities and support. 

 

Kids should come ready to learn, play, ride and explore!

Backpack examples 

A small pack that fits snugly and is just big enough to carry a water bottle and snacks, and maybe a small found treasure or two is great.

Welcome to the Cross Camp - four nights of cyclocross racing at the iconic Driveway in Austin, TX.

The rules are simple:

  1. Don’t be a jerk.
  2. Abide by all USAC cyclocross rules.
  3. The promoter’s ruling is final.
  4. Gravel and mountain bikes without bar ends are allowed. No maximum tire widths enforced.
  5. Please inform the finish line judges if you withdraw from the race.
  6. Prizes will be awarded 3 deep in competitive categories.
  7. Please patronize our sponsors.
  8. You must check in with the registration staff to be counted in the results.
  9. Absolutely no alochol is permitted on the grounds of The Driveway at any time. 


Entry Fees

Entry fees are $50 for your first race and includes any additional races on the same day (ex. Novice riders may also enter the 3/4 /Novice field on the same day at no additional cost).  Note: You must register for these at the same time to take advantage of this discount.

Season passes are available and will automatically enroll you for 4 nights of the category of your choosing. You may also select additional races throughout the series during your registration if you would like to race multiple categories on some (or all) nights.

Late registration is available this year. Entries after 12 pm the day of each race will incur a $5 late fee and may not be included in call ups. Registration closes 30 minutes before each race wave, so we highly encourage you to sign up as soon as you can!

Racing Licenses

All categories require a USA Cycling license to participate. If you do not have a current USAC annual license you can purchase one at memberships.usacycling.org. 

Course

You will race on +/- 1.5 mile courses taking in new trails connected by fast pavement for a course that's always changing.

 

Parking and directions

Ample parking is available at the Driveway, but we highly encourage you to ride to the races. Please drive slowly on Delwau Ln, respect the venue, their neighbors and be cognizant of bicycles and pedestrians.

Weather

The event is rain or shine. Delays or cancellations may be issued at the discretion of the promoter or race officials in the event of severe weather.

Introducing the fall Adirondack Women's Weekend featuring two incredible days of fully supported road cycling from the relaxing and cozy Lodge at Schroon Lake.

Dates: October 9-11  
Location: Schroon Lake  
Mileage: 15-32 miles/day  
Participation Cap: 10 riders  
Benefits: Schroon Lake Association

Since the June Adirondack Women's Weekend sells out annually, it's time to introduce an intimate boutique event for the fall with a maximum of 10 riders. And there's no better place to host it than the stunning Schroon Lake region and the incredible Lodge at Schroon Lake. Whether attending solo or with friends, this small group experience is all about fun, relaxation and having a great time, on and off your bike. Add in delicious dining, fun surprises and the blissful ease of knowing everything is taken care of and you've got a weekend of enjoying the best of the southern Adirondacks without the stress of planning. We make sure of that by providing professional cycling guides, fully stocked rest stops, a mechanic, and a support vehicle.

Highlights include a delicious Friday arrival dinner, happy hours on Friday and Saturday, two incredible fully supported road cycling routes and the camaraderie you can only get from a small group tour in the Adirondacks.

Need a teaser? Check out this video from one of our June events in Saranac Lake, which we've modeled this new event after.

Best of all, a portion of the event proceeds will support the Schroon Lake Association and their volunteer efforts to preserve, promote, and protect the welfare of Schroon Lake, the Schroon River, and the watershed area.

Registration Includes

  • 2 nights’ single or double accommodations
  • 2 fully supported & guided road cycling routes
  • Hearty rest stops
  • Secure bike parking
  • Exquisite dinner the night of arrival
  • Breakfast Saturday and Sunday
  • Event gifts & surprises  
     

Our Host

Lodge at Schroon Lake

This incredible property is a beautiful 36-acre resort on the west shore of Schroon Lake featuring 116 rooms, 32 of which are pet-friendly. It includes hotel rooms, standalone cabins and chalets, and upscale glamping sites. Plus, guests have access to a world-class restaurant and bar, miniature golf, multi-purpose sports courts, and a private beach with docks and a deck. Additional amenities include an indoor pool, a private marina, a game room, and lawn games.

Hassmer Fest 2026

Hassmer Fest is a three-day mountain bike festival is back for 2026! Enjoy the best mountain bike festival in Southeast Indiana.  Hassmer Fest is hosted within the beautiful Versailles State Park in Versailles, Indiana.  The trail system within the park offers miles of flowing single track, providing a great riding experience for all skill levels, from beginner to the most experienced. This year we celebrate thirteen years of the festival and nearly 30 miles of mountain trails. 

The park’s trail system exists due to the hard work and dedication of volunteers that have a love for mountain biking, as well as a love for the great outdoors.  Hundreds of volunteer hours are accrued each year to build and maintain the trail system.

All proceeds of Hassmer Fest go directly to support the efforts of the volunteer trail crew within Versailles State Park. Come out and enjoy a great weekend of riding, entertainment, and friendship.

Pre-Registration

Online Pre-Registration: $75.00 (March 1 - October 7, 2026)  

Day-of-Event Registration:  $90.00 - Cash, Check or Credit Card (via Square) at event site.

Ride-em-All Challenge - Pre-registration required

The Ride-em-All Challenge requires riders to ride nearly 30-miles of the trail system within Versailles State Park. 

Riders must ride with a punch card.  Punch cards can be claimed at registration area during the event. 

Ride-em-All signs are strategically placed on each of the trails within the mountain bike trail system. Each sign contains a unique orienteering punch.  Use the orienteering punch to mark your punch card accordingly.  

This is a pre-registration category only this year.  There is a fee of $20.00 to participate and receive your ride-em-all challenge hat. Please note this item a “trail” style hat from Cognative Mountain Biking. One size fits most!

October 10, 2026

9:00-11:00am

 

Who This Clinic is For
You have some experience mountain biking and would like to increase your skills beyond the basics. This course will teach beginner-intermediate riders the technique to execute more efficient and controlled riding. This clinic is for those aged 14 and older.

 

Clinic Overview

This is a 2-hour clinic with optional on-trail practice following.

You’ll Learn:

  • Safety checks to perform before each ride
  • Proper body position and maintaining balance while riding
  • Front and rear wheel awareness
  • Controlled cornering and switchback technique
  • Efficient climbing
  • Safely remounting and dismounting off the bike 
  • Important Info
  • All riders must wear a helmet and have a trail-ready bike in good working order.
  • Dress appropriately for the weather.
  • Bring your own water and snacks.
  • Minimum age to participate is 14 years old.

MTB Skills Clinic - Kids Beginner - Pre-registration required

October 10, 2026

11:00am-12:00 pm

 

Who This Clinic is For
Kids ages 6 and up who want to build the foundational skills of balance, confidence, and safety for fun and safe riding. 

 

Clinic Overview

This is a 1 hour clinic.

You’ll Learn

  • Safety checks to perform before each ride
  • Essentials for safe riding
  • Proper body position and maintaining balance while riding
  • Consistent brake control
  • Proper shifting to maintain speed

Important Information

  • All riders must wear a helmet and have a trail-ready bike in good working order. 
  • Dress appropriately for the weather.
  • Closed-toe shoes.
  • Bring your own water.

Entertainment

Event opens Friday, October 9 at 3:00PM.  Event concludes Sunday, October 11 at Noon. Participants must clear the event space by 5:00 PM on Sunday. EventName: Pumpkin Hop Cross 2026 - The Evolution of a SpeCXies
EventNotes:
NO RACING LICENSE IS REQUIRED TO ENTER & PARTICIPATE

All but the “first-timers” races require an entry fee.

Enter as many races for which you are qualified!  That means you can race within your category and higher, but not lower.  Races are gender-inclusive EXCEPT those designated "Women."  Those are...wait for it...just for the girls, but I'm not deciding for you what that means.  Juniors are not limited to the junior races.  Try those AND your category race if you want.  Just like single speed isn't limited to the single speed race.  Put that one-trick pony up against the geared machines in your category race and show 'em that gears don't mean a thang - it's cyclocross!  

Registration is online-preferred

Do this from any electronic, internet-equipped device you see fit, and that theoretically you own.  Use your preferred means of digital money, and voila!  You're in!  We can move stuff around on race-day or before if you need to make a change (see note on refunds below).  Let us know!  You can still register in person via Venmo or exact cash or check.  No set cut-off time before your race, but please be punctual and considerate of your registrar, official, and fellow racers.  The best way for all of us is online in advance. BikeReg closes at 4 p.m. Friday for the night race, then open for the rest of the weekend, AND you can register on site if your individual circumstance dictates. 

We plan to have the course open at 8:00 a.m. Saturday (7:00 on Sunday), with registration opening by 9:00 (8:00 on Sunday).  You'll likely use the same number all weekend, no matter the race.  This will depend, in part, on the number of registrants.

Licenses

NO RACING LICENSE REQUIRED.  This is not a USAC-sanctioned event this year.  We always hope more and more people get involved and it is an attempt at removing a potential barrier to entry.  Those of  you that do hold a license with USAC, keep up the good work!!!  Thank you, everyone, for your cyclocross ambassadorship!

Equipment

Run what you brung.  Ride what you can abide.  Bike what you like.  Wheel what you feel.  You do not have to have a cyclocross-specific steed.  You'll have a lot more fun if you at least have knobby tires, though.  That's pretty much a must.  As is a helmet.  We want you to have fun, but we need you to be safe, so you have to have a helmet and you have to wear it at all times while on your bike.

Staging & Starting Intervals

Staging is first-come, first-choice.  You know what time your race starts.  Just pay attention and play nice.  Yeah, we know you're strong and like that front row call up, but we also know you're going to be on the front before the hole shot, anyway.  You are a beast, after all.  Many of our races will have combined fields.  Our official(s) will determine the start time intervals and field order on race day.

Waivers

All participants or their parent/guardian (if under 18) must sign our waiver in-person at number pickup.

Podiums & Prizes

A podium presentation will occur as soon as possible following completion of each race.  Results typically are ready pretty quickly, so unless there is a protest - we've never had a protest; our officials are the tops - we'll get you called up for a picture and a prize post-haste.  We're awarding a total cash purse of an amount hopefully worth writing home about.  And it wouldn't be Pumpkin Hop Cross if we didn't give away a few pumpkins!

And pie.

RESULTS WILL BE UPLOADED TO CROSSRESULTS.COM

Refunds

Life happens.  Boy howdy, does it.  If you register, THANK YOU!!!  But then it turns out you can't come. If you want us to keep your money as a donation to the cause, THANK YOU!!!  If you would like to request a refund, THEN PLEASE DO!!!  We will miss you, absolutely, but you won't have to miss your cash for very long.  Sorry we can't refund BikeReg surcharges, though.  No refund requests will be considered after September 30th.

Rules

Our official(s) will be USA Cycling trained and experienced, so plan on abiding by USA Cycling rules. Check out usacycling.org if you need a review. Otherwise, be kind.  It supersedes all other rules, anyway.

CAMPING

When you register, please let us know if you’ll be camping with us, and if you will be pitching a tent or sleeping in your vehicle.  That will help us determine good locations for you and consider breakfast options, as well!  It is FREE to camp, of course.

Also known as "the ride for pie" this is one of the region's favorite cycling events known for its unique character and atmosphere.

Routes of 16, 25, 50, 62, and 100 miles will leave from Legislative Mall, 410 Legislative Ave., Dover, DE, and wind through central Delaware's peaceful (and flat!) Amish countryside. Featuring unique scenery, friendly volunteers, pie and fun for all. This ride is perfect for your first century!

This is not a timed event or race. 

Motor vehicles are not restricted on the routes of the Amish Country Bike Tour. Follow all rules of the road. Never cross a yellow line, not even to pass. 

To promote safety and relieve congestion, a staggered police escorted start based on distance is scheduled out of Dover:

Departure times:
Please leave at your assigned departure time based on your intended ride distance.

These departure times will provide police escorts from Dover and ensure that your rest stops are open:
  - 100 miles: 7:00 am, follow the WHITE arrows
  - 62 miles: 7:30 am, follow the RED arrows
  - 50 miles: 8:00 am, follow the GREEN arrows
  - 25 miles: 8:30 am, follow the BLUE arrows
  - 16 miles: 9:00 am, follow the YELLOW arrows

PLEASE note that ALL arrows leaving the start will be WHITE; the colors will change once the routes separate.

Leaving prior to your designated starting time is not recommended. Staggered start times are designed to reduce road congestion and ensure that rest stops are open at appropriate times. All participants must have completed their ride by 5 pm.

DATE AND LOCATION

The ride is on Saturday, October 10, 2026. Riders choosing the full event ticket can choose from four distance options (20, 29, 40, and 65 miles), each visiting some of the most scenic backroads in the region. 

 - Start and Finish for the 20-mile, 29-mile, 40-mile, and metric century routes:

Lancaster Elementary School, 191 School Road, Kilmarnock, VA 22482.

Newer and casual riders may register for a Beginner/Casual Ride, a 10-mile loop on quiet farm roads that starts and ends at historic Shiloh School.

- Start and Finish for the Beginner/Casual Ride:

Shiloh School, State Rte. 606, Kilmarnock, VA 22482

REGISTRATION FEES

20-mile, 29-mile, 40-mile, and metric century routes: $75

Beginner/Casual Ride: $50

Day-of Event surcharge (if offered), Registration fee + $15

WHAT DOES MY REGISTRATION COVER ?

Event insurance, rest stop food & drinks, advertising and logistics, and ride T-shirt.

A portion of your entry fee will benefit the Northern Neck Bike Club, a 501(c)3 nonprofit organization focused on building trails, mentoring youth, and empowering our community through cycling.

IS THERE A T-SHIRT FOR SALE?

Yes, each registrant will receive a T-shirt. You can purchase additional T-shirts for non-riding friends and family during registration.  

River Ride 2026 participants may also purchase a club-cut cycling jersey for $70 during registration.

Depending on size and quantity, T-shirts and jerseys purchased after Sept. 15 may be mailed to participants after the event.

THE ROUTES

The event will feature four course options: a 10-mile beginner/casual route, and main routes of 20, 29, 40 and 65 (metric century) miles. All routes wind through some of the most scenic and peaceful roads in Virginia’s Northern Neck.

RideWithGPS will be available to all participants, and the course will be marked with painted arrows before and after every turn. Preliminary maps are available here: River Ride 2026 Preliminary Routes. Final versions will be published the week prior to the event.

STOPS/TREATS/RIDE SUPPORT

Well-stocked rest stops will be available along the routes, each offering essential supplies and a warm, helpful team of volunteers.  Our SAG (Support and Gear) team will be monitoring the routes for your safety.

Afterwards, enjoy Kilmarnock’s Fall Festival at Town Centre Park, and then join us at That Damn Mary Brewing Company for the River Ride After Party from 6:00-8:00.

CAN I CHECK IN EARLY ?

Yes. We offer early check-in from 6:00pm–8:00pm on Friday, October 9 at Lancaster Elementary School.

WHEN CAN I CHECK IN ON RIDE DAY ?

Check-in opens at 6:30am at Lancaster Elementary School. Please park first, then come to the check-in table and pick up your t-shirt and rider packet. A ride concierge will be available answer questions about the routes and provide safety information. 

WHEN CAN I START THE RIDE?

Check-in opens at 6:30am and closes at 9:00 am.  

After checking in, riders depart at their own pace, but should plan their ride so they finish no later than 3:00pm. 

The last rest stop will close at 4:00pm.  Our support vehicles will sweep the course throughout the event day to ensure all riders return safely.

WHERE DO I PARK ?

Registration/Check-in/Main Ride: Please park at Lancaster Elementary School, or in the Town of Kilmarnock parking lot on the corner of West Church Street and School Street.

Beginner/Casual Ride: (Please check-in at Lancaster Elementary School before driving to the beginner/casual ride start). Park in the designated parking area at Shiloh School. Due to the heavy cycling traffic at this location, a volunteer will guide you to safely depart from the parking area when you have finished your ride.

ARE RESTROOMS AVAILABLE AT THE START? 

Yes, the elementary school has agreed to open restrooms during check-in and registration.  Additional port-a-potties will be provided, if needed.  

REFUNDS/DEFERRALS/TRANSFERS

As with most events of this caliber, there are no refunds. This is a rain or shine event. In the unlikely event that the ride must be canceled due to extreme weather (hurricanes, flooding, etc.), participants may receive credit toward registration for the make-up date, if scheduled, or toward the 2026 River Ride.

ARE E-BIKES ALLOWED?

Yes. Class 1 and Class 3 e-bikes are allowed because they are pedal-assisted.  Mopeds, scooters, and throttle-only e-bikes are not allowed.

ARE HELMETS REQUIRED ?

Yes.  An ANSI or SNELL certified helmet is required when riding a bike during this event.  All Virginia traffic laws must also be followed.

CAN MY YOUNG CHILDREN RIDE ALONG ?

River Ride 2026 includes a 10-mile beginner-friendly route that takes place on quiet farm roads; children under the age of 18 who participate in this route must be comfortable riding on open roads, and must be accompanied by a parent who must sign a waiver on their behalf. Children in baby seats or trailers are not permitted.

IS FOOD PROVIDED ?

Yes.  Every rest stop will be stocked with water and a variety of snacks. Also, the 20-, 29-, 40-, and 65-mile routes pass by convenience stores, farm markets, and agribusinesses that may be open on the day of the ride.

Riders planning to complete the metric century route should select a box lunch option during registration. That lunch will be ready for them at the lunch stop (Rice’s Hotel/Hughlett’s Tavern).

WHO DO I CONTACT IN CASE OF A CHALLENGE ALONG THE ROUTE ?

Because cell service can be limited, we strongly encourage riders to stay in groups.  If assistance is needed, call the number on your wristband at 804-480-2776.  Our team will locate and support you.  We also have volunteers and HAM radio operators driving the course to provide SAG support. If you need SAG support, please stay in a safe location along the route and watch for a SAG vehicle to come by.  

WHERE CAN I STAY OVERNIGHT ?

The Northern Neck has a wonderful variety of lodging options, from boutique hotels and waterfront rentals to world-class luxury lodging. Visit Virginia’s River Realm to learn more about lodging options for the ride weekend.

CAN I VOLUNTEER TO HELP?

Absolutely!  We’d love your support.  Please click here to contact the River Ride team directly.

The Filthy 50 is an annual gravel road cycling event that takes place on the gravel roads around Lanesboro, Minnesota on the second Saturday in October as the leaves on the trees begin to change. This is our 12th anniversary! There are 25 and 50 mile routes for our riders to choose from. All are welcome and encouraged. "Race it and set a record. Ride it and take in the beauty. Either way, get filthy." - Unknown

Check-In will run from 6pm - 8pm on Friday, October 9th at Sylvan Brewing and then again at Pedal Pushers Cafe from 7am - 9:00am on Saturday, October 10th. There are no additional check-in options nor are there any new "walk-up" registrations available at these times.

The Pretty Filthy 25 mile riders will leave downtown Lanesboro on Saturday, October 10th at 9:30am under police escort along with our 50 mile riders. They will follow the creek as they climb Grosbeak and Gentle eventually descending on Easy Street and then will turn south, following Gribben Creek out of the valley. After an epic return featuring Grit Road, it will be a hero’s welcome as they cross our finish line in the middle of downtown Lanesboro. This route features minimum maintenance roads, 1900+ feet of climbing, and some of the prettiest scenery you ever did see. If you haven’t attempted The Filthy before, we highly recommend that you start here.

The Filthy 50 mile riders will leave downtown Lanesboro on Saturday, October 10th at 9:30am under police escort, heading south and then east as they follow the creek climbing Grosbeak and Gentle then eventually descending on Easy Street. They will then climb the infamous Dew Drop and turn south towards “The Big Woods” and Amish country. These riders will want to consider their options when they reach Grub Hill and keep their wits about them when they hit the Amish maintained MMR just west of Henrytown. After making their way down Grit Road, crossing our finish line in downtown Lanesboro is gonna feel good. This route will feature several minimum maintenance roads, 3200+ feet of climbing, and perhaps a surprise or two along the way. It ain’t easy, but nothing worth doing ever is.

Route Details and more information can be found at https://the-filthy.com/

Lodging Options can be found at https://www.lanesboro.com/list/ql/lodging-travel-tourism-15 if you're looking for a place to stay for the weekend. Act fast because Lanesboro and Bluff Country rooms are filling up!

EventName: Brutiful Cape: Gravel Bike & Fat Bike Adventure Rides - Oct 24 & 100 Miles for Fat Bikes Oct 25
EventNotes:
These are incredible gravel and fat bike rides in an area where riders get to experience all sorts of cool trails, back roads, and dirt roads that weave their way all over the Cape! Riders who select gravel rides won't be riding on beaches. Those who select fat bike options will have the opportunity to experience awesome beach riding in addition to the cool mixed terrain that this area serves up and few people know about.

For all Saturday riders who aren't camping Friday evening: We have secured parking within 0.4 mile from the campground so it won't take long to get from your car to the start!

We're offering a camping option at checkout so you can stay overnight right at the ride start & end at a nice campground if you prefer.

The Cape at this time of year is serene, it's not yet closed, but it also doesn't have many people on the beaches or trails. Roads are quieter than they are during the summer as well. 

Get your friends together to spend a fun weekend camping, enjoying the peace of the Cape, and memorable riding!

Riders will enjoy hot coffee and tea in the morning before rolling out and seasonally appropriate food (a hearty meal) at the end of the ride  (read: hot food if it's a chilly day!) Around a hot fire in a comfortable setting.

Complete details are on the Ride Page.

Well my friends, we're BACK for year SEVEN!!   

As you may know,  the HBRN8R goes beyond being just a grassroots cycling event and embodies a self-supported (mostly) test of mental, physical, and spiritual fortitude that unites participants with lasting memories and sense of accomplishment.   It's a true small-town community event that is hosted on a working farm overlooking the most beautiful ridgeline and run by the most hardworking & beautiful people (Ben & Kim Bangs).  

But here's the deal -- I'm a one-man show (and have always been).  While I appreciate the same-day support I have received over the years from friends who stepped up, it takes an IMMENSE amount of work to organize this event solo. For those of you who have been in the past, the 2-day weekend was a thing and I am so grateful to everyone's support!! Imagine putting on a wedding for 200 people by yourself two days in a row.  Crazy, I  know.  

With that said, I'm going back to our original format from the first two years - a one-day one-course format of mixed terrain riding that combines gravel, class IV, single track, farm fields, sugarhouse roads, and minimal pavement into one route that is equal to whatever bike you throw at it.   While this is mainly a self supported ride (NOT A RACE & NOT TIMED), I'll still keep your fire stoked at a few feed zones with wood-fired maple syrup, ,my homemade pumpkin chocolate chip cookies, water, and other goodies.  My buddy Jon Rutherford of ROKO vehicles will once again be out there on his Moto making sure people don't decide to snuggle up with a cuddly bear on course.   When you return, we'll spoil you with incredible locally sourced post-ride food, homemade pressed wild apple cider, a massive bonfire you can see from space where you can share stories while drinking Vermont beer.   Oh, it's been a tradition to give teddy bears and maple syrup to the first & last female/male across the line.  

The Mixed Terrain Course: 55ish miles - Coming soon!!

RWGPS:
Strava: 
GPX File: 

Bring the family because camping is FREE beginning Friday evening (a donation is welcome to support the landowners Ben & Kim) with no reservations needed!  It's a BIG ASS field.   Ben usually gives the kiddo's a tractor ride at the start of the event and lets them play in hay bails.  Oh, and there are animals to feed!  

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

But BUT Chris, the Full Harvest??  What about the MTB race on Sunday?  
I hear you loud & clear, but an official race day is out of the cards for various reasons.  The Solution?  Design the ultimate single track mtb route, give you the GPS file, assign parameters (i.e. you have all day Sunday just as long as you start/finish in the same spot),  race the course as fast as you possibly can go, and upload your time to Strava or RWGPS.  Oh and to sweeten the pot, an optional donation to the overall prize pot of local goodies that will go to the top three female & male finishers.

Note: This is not an organized day.  No food, no drinks, no feeds. Everyone must have a valid Kingdom Trails day pass on Sunday.  You assume all risks and respsonibilities.  

The MTB Course: Coming Soon

TrailForks: 
GPX File: Will be attached to your participation email. 

IMPORTANT NOTE: If racing the mtb course on Sunday, you are responsible of getting to the start location.  If camping at the venue, our hosts expect you to be out Sunday morning, and then you're on your own. 
 

So yeah, that's it.   Sounds fun, right?  Join us!! :-)
 

Ciao ciao for now,
Chris Gagnon

Race Description:  The Mohican Forest Trail boasts a continuous 25-mile loop through the Mohican State Forest. This is arguably some of the finest single track in Ohio, home of the largest mountain bike race in Ohio, The Mohican Mountain Bike 100k and 100 Mile race. 

Race Info:  This OMBC series race will begin and ends at Mohican Adventures on State Rt. 3, located adjacent to the Mohican State Park.

MTB Race Start: Noon. MTB Wave Starts: E-Bike then Pro/Expert Men will begin at noon with all other 18 divisions starting two minutes apart. Everyone should be ready at Noon.

PARK WARNING FOR RACERS and COURSE MARSHALLS: "Racers must know that they are to yield to traffic as they would when out riding the trail on any other day and volunteers must be directed that they are not to stop cars on the roads under any circumstances." Mohican State Park

This is a self-supportive race. There will be water and Hammer Heed available at Trail head two (about halfway point) for Sport and Expert MTB Classes. There will be no water stations MTB Novice Class Racers.  

Registration:  Discounted entry before October 17 so please register early for race packet, food and beverage planning purposes.

Novice Youth 12-14, 8-11 just $20

In honor of Jarrod Bunk’s belief that the bike community can help to build a community in need, we bring back Higher Ground with the locals of Johnstown, the Pennsylvania Environmental Council, and the Community Foundation for the Alleghenies.

This will be a scenic tour with opportunities to connect with the natural beauty of the Laurel Highlands and bond with like-minded souls before and after in downtown Johnstown.

The goal is to keep the grassroots spirit of the original iterations of Higher Ground which showcased rugged routes throughout the surrounding Johnstown area. Expect to be greeted with punchy climbs, path-less-travelled trails, and a tour of the environmental wonders that are the Laurel Highlands and the Allegheny Mountains. 

Here are the routes that will be available:

  • Thirty: An out-and-back on the Path of the Flood and Staple Bend Tunnel trails to go to the Johnstown Flood Memorial Park (you'll ride through the dam that broke).
  • Forty: Heads north towards Hinkston Run Reservoir, then east on quiet paved roads before bombing down into Summerhill and into the Johnstown Flood Memorial Park (you'll ride through the dam that broke), and returning to Johnstown on the Path of the Flood and Staple Bend Tunnel trails.
  • Sixty: Does the Forty route back into Johnstown, then up into the Rager District climb & descent, and back into Johnstown.
  • Eighty: Does the Forty route back into Johnstown, and then UP into the forested Gamelands west of town and then back down to the rolling roads in the south before riding back to on the Jim Mayer Riverswalk and into Johnstown.
  • Hundo: Does the Forty route back into Johnstown and then UP into the forested Gamelands west of town and then back down to the rolling roads in the south before riding back to on the Jim Mayer Riverswalk to the Start/Finish and the last 20 miles go up into the Rager District climb & descent and back into Johnstown.

There will be aid station support and the start/finish venue will have food & drink available. All riders must check in & out so we know who's taking on which sections of the course.

To learn more about the history and purpose of Higher Ground, read this story on The Radavist from 2022.

Partners that are making Higher Ground happen include:

  • Pennsylvania Environmental Council
  • Community Foundation for the Alleghenies
  • Fat Jimmy's Outfiters
  • Thomas Automotive
  • New Trail Brewing
  • Endo TuneUp
  • Stan's
  • Nittany Mountain Works
  • Footdown.cc
  • Freeze Thaw Cycles
  • Hushmoney Bikes

Proceeds from Higher Ground will support The Women's Help Center and the Pennsylvania Interscholastic Cycling League.

Race 2 for the Rust Belt Ruckus is OOFF CX (one o four farms cyclocross) in Lockport!

One O Four Farm CX is a taped cyclocross course that meanders though old apple orchards, wildflowers and farm fields in the heart of Niagara County.

This course is so good we race it twice! As race 2 of the Rust Belt Ruckus Series and for race 5 the finalle. Jon and Shannon always change things up so the course feels new and fresh even if you've raced it (every single time) like I have… It's rolling, has perfectly apexed turns through orchards and farm fields like flying through a labyrinth, and some punchy techy parts back by the beaver sanctuary. It really doesn't get much more fun than this for a cyclocross course.

Non Sanctioned, no USAC license required

Registration, Entry Fees, & Licensing:  all registration and payment for this event, including race day registration, will be conducted through BikeReg.  Additional entries are offered at $20 ($25 on race day) when purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart.  If the entries are purchased separately during the pre-registration period, contact us for a partial refund; on event day a coupon code will be made available at the day-of registration table to achieve the same discounted price.  Entry fees will increase to $50 for adults and $30 for Juniors for race day registration, to reflect the day-of surcharge.  There will be no in-person sales at the event -- register online, either at home before coming out or on your phone at the event.  You MUST present your racing license (if you have one) or 1-Day receipt in order to be issued a bib, and you should also be prepared to show your confirmation email.  In order to expedite your entry, make sure you have completed the online waiver before approaching the day-of registration table.

This page will re-open for late/day-of registration by Saturday 10/24 at 8:30 AM.  Check-in at the venue will open around 7:30 AM on event day.  Check-in and registration for all races will close 15 minutes prior to the scheduled start of the race. There will be no exceptions made to this rule -- plan to show up timely for the race you want to enter.

 Any current National Cyclocross Champions shall be granted free entry, but must wear their national jersey in the class in which it was won.

A USA Cycling racing license is required for entry.  Riders who do not provide a USAC Annual racing license # at registration will be assessed an additional $15 for a Beginner 1-Day license.  This license is valid for entry only in fields that are open to Novice Men, Women, or Non-Binary riders.  For all other fields, you must present proof of an active USAC racing license (or a printed Authorization to Ride) showing your Cyclocross category and Racing Age.

Code of conduct: Racers and spectators are expected to abide by USA Cycling's code of conduct. Any behavior, sign, kit, etc., that discriminates on the basis of race, color, religion, age, gender, sexual orientation, gender identification, or national origin, or that interferes physically with any race, will be met with ejection from the venue and disqualification from all races.

Gender Equality & Transgender Policy: Classes designated “Masters” are open to Men and Women. The minimum Racing Age and categories quoted are for Men; please see the current USAC Rulebook for minimum Racing Age and categories for Women.  The Super Series  welcomes everyone to participate in the gender category they feel is most appropriate to them, as described in USA Cycling policies: https://usacycling.org/about-us/governance/transgender-athletes-policy

The collective teams comprising the MABRA Super Series are committed to providing inclusive and equitable racing events.  The Super Series is proudly adding non-binary categories (1/2/3 and 4/5) to race during the women's races.  This addition is to honor all of our cyclists and provide a category that allows everyone to race with how they identify.  In the event that USAC chooses to amend current policy to align with UCI changes for our transgender racers, then WTF (women-trans-femme) will be added to our non-binary categories as WTFNB.

E-BIKE REGULATIONS (THIS IS A WORK IN PROGRESS....LEARNING AS WE GO....)
As we continue to provide e-bike racing in the Month of Mud series we want it to be a safe but welcoming racing environment for all mountain bike enthusiasts and racers. In order to do so we believe the following standards are fair for our local grassroots series.
 
• E- Bikes that are USAC UCI or GNCC certified are legal.
• E-Bikes must pedal assist with a max speed of 20mph.
• Programmable E-Bikes must be set and locked to 750 watts and 20 MPH. • Throttle mechanisms are prohibited. • Boost buttons must be removed or disabled. • No aftermarket modifications will be allowed.
• E-Bikes must be inspected 30 minutes before the race start. • E-Bikes MUST be in the off position at the starting line and powered up at the official's instructions. • Settings must be verified immediately after finishing. • Any E-Bike that is found to be illegal, rider will forfeit all prizes and points and will be suspended for remaining races. All categories. • Officials carry the right to test any E-Bike in question. Month of mud is not liable for any damage that may occur during testing. If you withhold your E-Bike to this test, you will be disqualified from the race.
• Passing etiquette must be followed. Unsportsmanlike behavior, foul riding, use of profanity, or flagrant discourtesy directed at participants, spectators, or officials will result in disqualification.
• Analog bikes have the right of way, you must yield to a racer in a different class to pass you when appropriate and safe to do so.
• No battery swapping during the race

PLEASE CHECK INDIVIDUAL RACE EVENTS ON BIKE REG, WEBSITE AND FACEBOOK GROUP FOR RACE TIMES & MORE DETAILS AS EACH RACE APPROACHES.

Please read this!
 

Welcome to our FREE monthly ride! Ride start times vary by season to give us the best trail conditions and safest experience—May through September we roll out at 9:00 AM CT, and October through April we begin at 2:00 PM CT. We meet at the lower parking lot at Turkey Mountain Urban Wilderness Park, 6800 S Elwood Ave, Tulsa, OK 74132. Restrooms are available.

 

We will have ride leaders for skill levels between Beginner to Advanced. If you're new to mountain biking, OR have never taken WeROK’s Fundamentals, or other formal fundamentals skills clinics (even if you have been riding some), we REQUIRE YOU to start with the WeROK Fundamental Skills Session during registration. Regardless of your riding experience we feel taking this skills session will help improve your riding and create a better riding experience for all.

 

Loaner Bikes: Please refer to your registration confirmation letter. 
 

Cancellation/Bad Weather Policy: If bad weather develops we aim to cancel the event by 7:00 am the day of the ride.  Stay tuned to social media for announcements. We also follow Trailbot, in case Turkey Mountain trails are “closed” or “delayed”.  We do not have “rain dates”. 

 

Choosing appropriate group: First choose your riding and fitness level, then choose the best description among the groups. Once a group fills, the waitlist option will open. If you have a friend with the same skill level with whom you want to ride, help us out by registering together ASAP, in the same ride level, AND in same group number. Other than cancellations, we CANNOT GUARANTEE we can make any changes to groups, especially at the last minute, since we have group size restrictions. This delivers the best possible ride experience for all! If you don't end up riding with your friends, don't worry, you'll have the opportunity to make new ones!
 

Not sure which group to join? Ride levels are based on YOUR CURRENT skill and endurance levels. We want everyone to have the best and safest experience possible so we use a “rating” system to help align you with the right ride group. Please review the skills, endurance, mileage and proposed trails. Being in the right group makes a better, safer ride for all. If you are still unsure about which group might be for you just contact us at ride@werok.org. P.S. It is perfectly fine to “repeat” a level! Mastery of ALL levels takes time and practice. Please don’t rush yourself, nor succumb to peer pressure. NOTE: WeROK’s skill level names and colors are relative to Turkey Mountain trails. Other trail systems’ color designations could mean their Blue is (y)our Black, so be wise!
 

Advancing to next groups: A great way to know if you are ready to progress to the next ride level is if (1) you felt comfortable with skills necessary at your current level, and (2) you were able to keep up with the ride leader the entire ride and felt like you could have ridden longer. 

 

GROUP CHOICES:
 

1. FUNDAMENTAL SKILLS SESSION 

Select this group if you have never ridden a mountain bike, it’s been longer than you’d like to admit, OR you've never taken any type of basic mtb skills lessons before. Welcome! You have to start somewhere and this is the place! Even the most advanced riders should brush up on these essentials, and certainly, if you feel rusty, this session will help you. This session will cover the fundamentals of mountain biking, and then you'll hit the trail for a 2-3 mile ride. Successful completion of WeROK’s Fundamentals (or its equivalent) is required for advancement to next groups. Departure from this policy requires approval by a WeROK ride leader.

  • Skill Level: Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals are required (we may have loaner pedals available; email us ahead of time at ride@werok.org).
  • Skills you can perform: no requirement, you will definitely learn a skill or two after this session. 
  • Fitness Level: No requirement other than participate in possible heat for up to 2 hours.
  • Example of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, no rocks; double track near Bomb Cellar; the grassy fields; the Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop. 

2. FUNDAMENTALS TO GREEN Group

Select this group if you have taken the Fundamental Skills session, you feel more confident with those skills, and you are looking for a very easy-going transition to green trails. You will have a skills refresher for up to 15 minutes.

  • Skill Level: Confident Beginner.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals strongly encouraged (see above re: loaner pedals).
  • Skills you can perform: Staying upright while pedaling, skills learned in Fundamentals Group are beginning to make sense, and your confidence is growing.
  • Fitness Level: Completed a Fundamentals session with minimal fatigue
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with occasional flat, mellow rocks or roots, no significant downhill or uphill; Family Loop; the lower “mini-switchback-berm” loop; the very first section of LoChi Connector.
  • Duration: 3-5 miles, maybe longer in cooler weather, no longer than 1.5 hours after refresher portion

3. GREEN Group
You’ve ridden on the dirt trails multiple times by now, and you’re getting the hang of things. You’re mastering the Fundamentals Skills, and your bike operating and handling skills feel smoother. No Fundamentals refresher portion provided.

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: Level pedals while coasting; one finger braking; becoming more comfortable with neutral and ready positions; and smoother corners/berms.
  • Fitness level: Able to ride steady at a comfortable pace for 30 minutes on easy terrain, and may need a breather while climbing, or at the top.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt with a variety of low, smooth surface changes; more variety of up and downhill; LoChi; UHF or All Up with rests.
  • Duration: 5-7 miles,1.5 to 2.0 hours 

4. OPEN Group

Looking for new challenges! You are ready to explore more trail features (obstacles) and a variety of up and downhills, with limited stops. Mileage varies. No Fundamentals refresher provided. 

  • Skill level: Beginner Plus-to-Intermediate.
  • Pedals: Flat pedals preferred.
  • Skills you can perform: GREEN skills are solid, but you’re out of saddle more instinctively with level pedals; in and out of neutral/ready position more smoothly; frequent appropriate shifting; smoother, smoother berms and corners; want to ride across straight bridges and skinnies 3-5 feet wide; comfortable choosing lines through rockier terrain, or between tight trees.
  • Fitness level: You’re riding a few times a week. Can ride a WeROK course continuously unless learning steep or more technical terrain. Pushing the pace uphill.
  • Examples of Turkey Mountain terrain: Packed dirt, more roots and rocks, twists and turns. The small bridge on OLD Lo Chi, All Up, UHF, Stay Gold Loop, Naharkey clockwise, maybe counterclockwise. Sessioning features within your skill set, such as the small skinny on Family Loop.
  • Duration: 8-10 miles, 2 hours with some stopping.

EventName: The Ride Series MTB Skills Clinics: JUMP BASICS & JUMP PROGRESSION SUN OCT 25th
EventNotes:
The Ride Series is different. Your expectations should be high as you enter the hospitality of our classroom setting. A comfortable Kijaro chair awaits your presence and the cover our 10x20 tents provides reprieve from the elements. Prepare yourself to be immersed in an environment that provides the perfect opportunity for you to be open to embracing and practicing the proper technique. Instant feedback from our coaching staff will have you progressing like never before! Are YOU ready??

 

 

 

JUMP BASICS: 

We get it, everyone wants to jump! However, most people don't embrace the technique AND psychology behind doing it well. You have to understand the what and why before you can start to build confidence with the how, that's what this session is for. Not only will you build a solid understanding of what NEEDS to happen, you'll also get plenty of reps working through the steps of how it needs to happen, all in a safe and controlled environment. 

Topics Covered: 

Riders will get plenty of reps on multiple takeoffs/landings and Rich will work through multiple rounds of video so you can see exactly what's working and what isn't. 

JUMP PROGRESSION Session: Ground School and Skills Park Jumpline

This event is all about getting comfortable in the air. That starts with a solid understanding of what it takes to get into the air properly. It's also critical to get as MANY reps as possible in a controlled environment and that's what the TRS ground school setting gives you.

Our Pro level coaches break down the dynamics involved with jumping a bike. Based on over 70 years experience, they guide you through their real world experience and give you key insight and cues on what to do and also what not to do. 

After showcasing the proper technique, you'll work through a series of reps and the distance will incrementally increase as your comfort level increases. Analysis and feedback using slow motion video will have you "busting big" in no time.

There's no substitute for experience when it comes to jumping a bike. The only problem is that experience in the right setting can be hard to come by. You'll get tons reps on our jump lines and receive valuable feedback in the moment.
RIDERS MUST HAVE:
- Experience jumping
- Full suspension bikes with suspension in working order
- Full safety gear including pads (Full Face helmet not required, but suggested)

This class is intended for riders with jump experience and will move at a specified pace. Coaching staff reserves the right to hold riders to pre determined distances based on performance.

Please reach out if you are unsure if this class is a proper fit for you.

Adventure Cycling Association is celebrating 50 years of bicycle travel in 2026. To mark this milestone, we invite you to join the 50TH ANNIVERSARY DROP-IN RIDES, a celebration across three legendary routes.

WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF THE DROP-IN RIDES?
Drop-In Rides are part of Adventure Cycling’s 50th Anniversary. Just as Bikecentennial ’76 sparked a movement 50 years ago, these rides celebrate where we started, what we’ve accomplished, and where we’re going—inviting riders everywhere to share in the adventure.

THE ROUTES
TRANSAMERICA TRAIL – The original Bikecentennial ’76 route that launched Adventure Cycling. Nearly 4,200 miles from Oregon to Virginia, it passes through small towns, farmland, the Rockies, and Appalachians. Dropping in here connects you with the history of cross-country cycling.

GREAT DIVIDE MOUNTAIN BIKE ROUTE – Since 1998, the world’s premier off-pavement route. Over 2,700 miles of gravel, dirt, and rugged mountain passes from Montana to New Mexico. A true test of endurance and adventure, inspiring riders worldwide.

GOLDEN GRAVEL TRAIL – Created for our 50th Anniversary, debuting in 2026. A mixed-surface journey across plains, canyons, and mountains, designed to showcase America’s growing gravel culture and the future of bicycle travel.

WHERE CAN I LEARN MORE ABOUT THE ROUTES?
Visit our route overview pages to see descriptions, maps, and details to help you choose the ride that fits your goals:

  • Great Divide Mountain Bike Route overview
  • TransAmerica Trail overview
  • Golden Gravel Trail overview (launching early 2026)

HOW DO I GET MY ROUTE AND NAVIGATE IT?
Adventure Cycling offers both paper maps and digital maps for purchase:

  • TransAmerica Trail Maps
  • Great Divide Maps

These maps include turn-by-turn directions, service listings, and detailed navigation notes. Once downloaded, digital maps can be used offline on your GPS device or phone.

Golden Gravel Trail Maps – This brand-new 50th Anniversary route will be free to download starting early 2026.

For more information about digital maps, visit our Digital Routes FAQ.

HOW CAN I FIND A GROUP TO RIDE WITH?
Check out our Companions Wanted listings to connect with others planning to ride.

Adventure Cycling members can post on Companions Wanted (become a member, just $2.50/month), while anyone can respond to a post. Drop-In Rides have a dedicated section in Companions Wanted in celebration of our 50th Anniversary.

EventNotes:
2026 I Love Gravel Racing Points Series

Everyone, Everywhere, Every distance

3 distance categories

Short = 24 miles or less, Mid = 25-49 miles, Long = 50+ miles

 

A different approach to a Points Series. There will be 2 categories, Male and Female, no age group, NO E-BIKES. Must be a GRAVEL RACE. No minimum or maximum number of races. No specific races, but Premier Races benefit the participant with double points.

For 2026 we have added Clydesdale and Athena categories. In addition, we will have the Fat Tire and Junior categories that were added in 2025. These categories will have a registration fee of $20 and do not include the opportunity to win FREE, or discounted, race entries. It does include your opportunity to win trophies, swag bags and your private invitation to the Champions Celebration. All details for these new categories are listed below.

Our goal is to increase participation in gravel racing. We are not looking for the fastest Champion. We would like our Champions to be passionate, and engaged, in the gravel racing community. With that thought in mind, the person who participates at more races stands a greater chance of being Champion.

Series will run from March 1, 2026 and end on November 1, 2026. You may sign up for the Series at any point throughout the year, but your points will not count until AFTER you have signed up. No retro results.

**Race results reporting are the responsibility of the participant. Participant must report their results to ILGR through an email (ILoveGravelRacing@aol.com) with a verifiable source, such as timing service or results documentation. Results must be reported within 2 weeks of race completion AND by November 1, 2026.**

$25 fee for registration will include your chance at the Championship. You are not locked into one distance. Your registration will allow you to compete in EVERY distance. 

Points will be awarded for your Overall Male or Female finish at ANY GRAVEL RACE, ANYWHERE. However, we have a group of Premier Gravel Races where double points may be earned. Since we have membership internationally, you may race anywhere, at any distance and participate in this Series.

Please contact ABRT via our website (http://abrtcycling.com) or email (abrtcycling@gmail.com) to determine if ABRT is a good fit for you. Our website lists rides/times/locations where you can meet and ride with our team.

ABRT isn't just for Seniors and Masters athletes.  We welcome Juniors of any experience and ability.  All that's required is an interest in bike racing and a willingness to learn.  Let us know you're interested and we'll direct you to the Junior Team Captain for more information on ABRT Junior programs.

Membership Information: 

We have a variety of membership types and membership programs. Please see our membership page for details: http://abrtcycling.com/about/membership

Delinquent Volunteering Fee:

The volunteer efforts are an integral part of what sustains ABRT. Members who were unable to fulfill the volunteer requirement the previous year are requested to select a second duty day or pay a delinquent volunteer fee of $50 prior to re-registering for this year.

A member not found to be in good standing (violation of the code or conduct or volunteer requirements) may forfeit race reimbursements and face expulsion from the team.

ABRT members except non-resident members cannot be a member of another USAC sanctioned team (see: http://www.usacycling.org/clubs/clubsearch.php) without the expressed consent from the ABRT Board of Directors.

EventName: 2026 Big Bear Lake Trail Center (WV) Merchandise
EventNotes:
The Big Bear Lake Trail Center is quickly becoming known as the hot spot for classic east coast single track. Years of trail development, by experienced mountain bikers have created a trail system that will have you grinning ear to ear. The terrain has everything to offer; gradual climbs, large embedded rocks, tight slaloms, challenging rock gardens, and off the saddle downhills. Almost 50 miles of trail wind through knee deep ferns, soft needle pine plantations, and groves of mountain laurel. Riders of all ages and abilities will find trails to fit their individual riding skills and need for adrenaline. The Big Bear Lake Trail Center is the place to bring the entire family to experience mountain biking at its best.

We make it easy to find your way around. Trail maps will be mailed to online season pass purchasers or you can ask for one at the main entrance.  We also suggest checking out the TrailForks app or the MTB Project app on your mobile device. Trail fees are $10/day or $30 for a season pass. Season passes will be mailed to you. If you choose to buy a day pass - bring proof of purchase in the form of a printed confirmation email or a screenshot on your phone. A staff member will verify that your pass is valid for that day.

All trails may be used for hiking, trail running, and x-c skiing. Trails are closed from November 1 thtough December 31. Trails are open from January 1 to October 31 each year.

Visit our WEBSITE.

Check us out on FB HERE or our events page HERE.

Cyclists enjoying trails at The Big Bear Lake Trail Center may inquire about overnight camping sites in Beaver Creek Village.

We do not close the trails due to wet conditions.

General Information

  1. Trails are open Jan 1 to Oct 31
  2. Both season and day passes must be purchased online
  3. Day fee is $10.00 per rider per day
  4. Season pass $30.00 (BEST VALUE!)
  5. Large color map included in fee.
  6. Children 12 and under free.
  7. Camping available at Beaver Creek Village sites. Inquire at Guard House or Office or online HERE.
  8. Helmets and personal safety equipment required.
  9. All riders must sign a release of liability form.  

Please contact us with any questions: (301) 501-1516, bikebigbearwv@gmail.com

Liability Waiver Statement: With the purchase of or use of a Big Bear Lake Trail Center season or day pass you agree to hold Alyeka, Inc. and the Bikg Bear Lake POA harmless and acknoledge the risks associated with trail use at the Big Bear Lake Trail Center.

The series takes place in the Quad Cities which is located on the Iowa Illinois border, nestled between the Mississippi River and Rock River.

Hell of the Wind- March 28th, New Liberty, IA

1904- April 25th, Morrison, IL

Gravel Riding Series Competition-

For the first time ever, the Big River Gravel Series will have an overall series payout for the top 3 men and women in the Mississippi distance. In order to be eligible for the payout a rider must sign up for the entire series using the Big River Gravel Series registration page. It is a dynamic payout. If 50 or less riders register for the Mississippi distance series the payout will be $500. For every rider who registers for the Mississippi distance once over 50 riders, the payout increases by $50 per rider registered. Example- 100 total riders register for the Mississippi distance series, the payout would be $3,000. 

Riders must decide if they want to compete in the Mississippi River (long distance) or the Rock River (short distance) for the series and stick with that distance for the entire series. If a rider switches distances, their points will start not carry over to the new distance series competition. 

The Big River Gravel Series will have an overall series payout for the top 3 men and women in the Mississippi distance. In order to be eligible for the payout a rider must sign up for the entire series using the Big River Gravel Series registration page on BikeReg. The rider must also finish all 4 events.

There will be a series competition for overall (women/men) in each distance, age group (women/men), and a single speed open. Riders are eligible for both point series competitions. 
 
There will be a podium for top three overall (women/men) in each distance and top three in each age group (women/men). Riders are eligible for both the overall and age group podium.

Age group categories are divided as follows. There will be an age group category for women and men. 19 and under juniors, 20-44, and 45+. 
 
Scoring for the overall and age group categories will work as follows. 1st= 10 points, 2nd= 9 points, 3rd= 8 points, 4th= 7 points, 5th= 6 points, 6th= 5 points, 7th= 4 points, 8th= 3 points, 9th= 2 points, 10th= 1 point

Scoring for the series will be based on a riders accumulative points from all 4 events. 

A rider must complete at least 3 of the 4 events to be eligible for the series. 
 
In the event of a tie at the end of the series, the tiebreaker will be determined by the rider who had the best result at the Turkey Burner.

EventNotes:
Get Ready for Revenant Cross Weekend!
Presented by ATC Racing | DNA Cycling

We're kicking off the cyclocross season with Revenant Cross at Richard Moya Park in Austin, TX – the TXCX series and season opener you don’t want to miss! With CX Nationals in Fayetteville, AR Dec 10–14, 2025, race with us now to earn USA Cycling points and improve your starting position there.

Expect a course that’s as fun as it is fierce – packed with off-camber turns, punchy climbs, and fast, flowy sections that'll keep your heart racing and your tires turning.

Spectators, this one's for you too! This course is super viewer-friendly, so bring your cowbells, cheers, and your best heckles – racers love it.

New to cyclocross? No worries – we’ve got a race category for everyone, from first-timers to seasoned CX pros. Come race, cheer, hang out, and be part of the scene.

Steady Rider Collective is covering women’s entry fees at Revenant Cross. Please spread the word, share our link, and join us for a fun-filled weekend. 

Cyclocross is the perfect way to sharpen your bike skills, test your grit, and most importantly – have an absolute blast doing it.

Sign up now, rally your riding buddies, and get ready for a weekend of mud, sweat, and cheers!

Revenant Cross Weekend is calling – will you answer?

Follow us on Social Media to stay up to date on Revenant Cross!

Instagram:  atc_racing_atx

TikTok: atc_racing_atx

Race rules:

  1. Don’t be a jerk.
  2. Abide by all USAC cyclocross rules.
  3. The promoter’s ruling is final.
  4. Gravel and mountain bikes without bar ends are allowed. No maximum tire widths enforced. 
  5. Please inform the finish line judges if you withdraw from the race. 
  6. Awards will be awarded 3 deep in competitive categories. Depending on field size, promoter may expand to 5 deep.
  7. Please patronize our sponsors.
  8. You must check in with the registration staff to be counted in the results.

 

Entry Fees

Entry fee is $40 for your first race and includes any additional races on the same day (ex. Novice riders may also enter the 3/4/Novice field on the same day at no additional cost).  Note: You must register for these at the same time to take advantage of this discount.

On-site registration will be available this year. Entries after midnight on Thursday 9/25 will incur a $10 late fee and may not be included in call-ups. Registration closes 30 minutes before each race wave, so we highly encourage you to sign up as soon as you can. Call-ups will be by crossresults.com.

 

Racing Licenses

All competitive categories require a USA Cycling license to participate. If you do not have a current USAC annual license you can purchase one at memberships.usacycling.org. Licenses are good for a period of one-year and covers road, mountain, gravel, track and cyclocross racing. If you get your license now, you'll be prepared for the rest of the TXCX series.

 

Parking and Directions

Ample parking is available in the lots at Richard Moya Park for no additional fee. Please respect park speed limits and be cognizant of bicycles and pedestrians inside the park. 

 

Weather

The event is rain or shine. Delays or cancellations may be issued at the discretion of the promoter or race officials in the event of severe weather.

 

Mechanical Support

Austin Tri Cyclist will be on-hand with neutral mechanical support all weekend. Conveniently located near the pit in case you need any mid-race fixes.
